$schema_note: Combined verified cross-KG joins for the Proto-OKN federation. Merges the A-I clusters with the spoke-okn geolocation crosswalks: cluster J (ZIP, on spoke-okn's full ~42,724-ZIP set) and cluster K (county/state FIPS, including spoke-okn's attachment to the SAWGraph spatial hub). Duplicates removed. Counts are exact COUNT(DISTINCT) over the named graphs on the verified_on date, EXCEPT cluster O (ufokn), whose verified_count is a SAMPLED lower bound (ufokn is too large for an exact full-graph count within the 120s endpoint limit) - see its verified_count_note. A consumer keyed by KG shortname should surface, for a given shortname, every entry where it appears as left_kg, right_kg, or bridge_kg. Clusters: (A) disease/phenotype - oard-kg is the MONDO/HP hub joining prokn, rdkg, nde and ubergraph; spoke-okn attaches via its 180 DOID Disease nodes (DIRECTLY to the DOID carriers prokn/biomarkerkg/nde, A7-A9, and through an ubergraph DOID->MONDO bridge to rdkg/oard-kg, A10-A11), (B) CAS chemical, (C) gene cluster - keyed across THREE id systems: Entrez/NCBI Gene (spoke-okn, spoke-genelab, rdkg, biobricks-aopwiki; in three IRI forms - see C_gene_cluster note - joined by bare-id rebuild; C4-C8), Ensembl (gene-expression-atlas-okn, pankgraph, spoke-okn's schema/ensembl crosswalk, AOP-Wiki; C1-C3, F1-F2), and HGNC (prokn, bridged to Entrez through wikidata P354->P351; C9), (D) SAWGraph S2 spatial hub, (E) toxicology/AOP CAS, (F) AOP-Wiki gene bridge, (G) UniProt protein, (H) soil-carbon spatial leaf (sockg: H1 S2 + H2 county to the spatialkg hub, plus H3 a DIRECT leaf-to-leaf S2 co-location with sawgraph's national US-WQP samples in 2 cells), (I) manufacturing supply-chain, (J) spoke-okn ZIP geography, (K) spoke-okn county/state-FIPS geography. (L) county/state-FIPS attachments of geoconnex, scales and nikg to the SAWGraph spatial hub (spatialkg) and spoke-okn, each carrying the same KWG/FIPS county key under a different non-obvious encoding (geoconnex: geoconnex.us/ref/counties/{FIPS5} reference IRIs on the GNIS county predicate; scales: a NUMERIC hasIdbCounty literal with the leading zero dropped; nikg: a phila.gov-rewritten KWG sfWithin IRI). Cluster L SUPERSEDES three base-file verdicts: scales (was an island on the unpopulated fips:CountyCode field), nikg (was 'no geographic key at all'), and geoconnex (only non-joins were recorded - its S2-cell and SAWGraph PWS reference-IRI non-joins remain valid, but the county-FIPS key is a separate, working route to the hub). Four further KGs profiled for cluster L (medical-device-kg, phaseskg, nasa-gesdisc-kg, wildlifekn) share no materialized join key and are recorded as islands / thin threads. (M) biobricks-mesh: the NLM MeSH vocabulary attaches to ubergraph on MeSH descriptor ids (oboInOwl:hasDbXref 'MESH:{ID}'), 9,463 matches dominated by MONDO disease (8,202), making it a MeSH-keyed member of the disease cluster A; biobricks-pubchem-annotations was profiled in the same pass and is an island (keyed solely on PubChem CID, which no federation KG materializes). Additionally biobricks-mesh has a second, DIRECT MeSH route (M2): spoke-okn MeSH-tags ~165 of its Disease and SDoH nodes via mesh_ids/mesh_list (HTTPS mesh IRIs vs biobricks-mesh's HTTP), uniquely reaching spoke-okn's social-determinants layer that the MONDO route (M1) cannot. (N) fiokg (SAWGraph FRS KG): a full SAWGraph spatial leaf attaching to the spatialkg hub via owl:sameAs to native KWG IRIs - 681,045 S2 Level-13 cells (N1, the LARGEST S2 join in the federation) and 3,031 county-FIPS AdministrativeRegion_2 IRIs (N2; 3,032 to spoke-okn, N3) - and to the manufacturing cluster I on the bare 6-digit NAICS code (N4 sudokn 64/66, N5 securechainkg 301/301). fiokg and the sawgraph leaf OVERLAP directly in 4,712 Maine S2 cells (N6, leaf-to-leaf), useful because fiokg flags 188,057 EPA-PFAS-Facility instances against sawgraph's PFAS samples. fiokg attaches at the county + S2 levels only (no KWG state IRIs); 261 leading-zero-truncated admin IRIs are excluded (see known_non_joins). (O) ufokn (Urban Flooding OKN): a FIFTH SAWGraph S2-cell spatial leaf. ufokn encodes its S2 cells as BLANK NODES (typed schema:PropertyValue + its own kwg:S2Cell ontology class), not KWG resource IRIs, with the 64-bit S2 cell id held as a bare decimal string in schema:value - the IDENTICAL value spatialkg uses as the suffix of its s2.level13.{id} node IRI. Rebuilding that IRI joins ufokn DIRECTLY to spatialkg's S2Cell_Level13 nodes (O1, no value rewrite). Three type-bounded samples (1k/8k/20k cells) all show 100% containment of ufokn's level-13 cells in spatialkg, so this is a near-complete attachment whose exact cardinality is not enumerable within the endpoint limit (verified_count 7,670 is a sampled lower bound). Cluster O SUPERSEDES the base file's two ufokn non-join verdicts ('unprofiled-large' and 'S2 Level-13 = 0'): the 0 was a direct typed-NODE join against blank nodes (can never match) and the timeout was an unbounded scan of ufokn's ~11.7M S2 nodes. ufokn also carries finer S2 LEVEL-18 cells that nest inside the level-13 hub cells but do not attach to the (level-13) hub directly. (P) biobricks-pubchem-annotations PubChem CID -> spoke-okn: spoke-okn materializes the CID as oboInOwl:hasDbXref identifiers.org/pubchem.compound/{n} on its ChemicalEntity nodes (762, exact 100% join after bare-CID normalization), SUPERSEDING the base file's biobricks-pubchem-annotations island verdict - it never checked spoke-okn's hasDbXref. (BH) biohealth (Bio-Health KG, UVA): a UMLS-CUI-keyed health graph (biomedical + social determinants) whose entities ARE their own https://biohealthkg.proto-okn.net/kg/node/C{cui} IRIs and which carries no outbound xref. It attaches ONLY through ubergraph's inbound UMLS hasDbXref on MONDO (10,087 biohealth CUIs), HP (4,828) and UBERON (2,148) - no CHEBI/UniProt/NCBIGene/NCIT UMLS xref exists, so biohealth crosswalks on disease, phenotype and anatomy only (never chemicals/genes/proteins). Verified joins BH1-BH8: rdkg, prokn, spoke-okn (via MONDO->DOID), oard-kg (MONDO + HP), nde, biomarkerkg (via MONDO->DOID) and gene-expression-atlas-okn. The UBERON anatomy axis is VERIFIED (BH9 biohealth<->GXA 249, BH10 biohealth<->spoke-genelab 35); spoke-okn stores no raw obo/UBERON_ terms and chemicals/genes/proteins remain unreachable. CL is not a biohealth axis (UMLS->CL = 0). biohealth is additionally a fragile LABEL-BRIDGED organism member of the taxon_hub (no NCBITaxon ids). See cluster_notes.BH_biohealth_umls. (AN) Anatomy (UBERON): spoke-genelab (INVESTIGATED_ASiA, 42 terms; + 7 CL cell types) and gene-expression-atlas-okn (biolink:has_attribute, 362 terms) carry raw obo/UBERON_ anatomy and join directly (AN1, 27 shared); biohealth attaches via the ubergraph UMLS->UBERON bridge (BH9/BH10). See cluster_notes.AN_anatomy_uberon.
$count_note: INTERNAL maintainer note - NOT user-facing. The single user-facing crosswalk count is len(all_crosswalks()) in src/mcp_okn/crosswalks.py - exactly what the list_crosswalks tool returns and what the README, the inventory doc (docs/crosswalks/proto-okn-crosswalk-inventory.md) and the network diagram cite. Do NOT surface the raw length of this verified_crosswalks array to end users: it is an internal storage count that differs from the user-facing number because all_crosswalks() (a) drops the ubergraph hub-scaffolding rows where ubergraph is a bare endpoint (e.g. A6 MONDO-expansion, M1 MeSH<->ubergraph) plus the compressed NCBITaxon hub rows, and (b) re-expands taxon_hub.pairwise into one row per KG pair. That derivation - not any number hardcoded here - is the source of truth, so this note never needs a count update. tests/test_crosswalks.py pins the user-facing docs to len(all_crosswalks()).

taxon_hub.$note: Materialized pairwise NCBITaxon overlaps between the hub member KGs (each maps organisms to ubergraph; crosswalks D3-D10). Each record is a non-zero pair {kg_a, kg_b, exact_id, clade_a_in_b, clade_b_in_a}: exact_id = same NCBITaxon id on both sides (symmetric); clade_a_in_b = kg_a taxa nested under kg_b's clades via ubergraph subClassOf* (directional), clade_b_in_a the reverse. Zero-overlap pairs are omitted. Regenerate with scripts/refresh_taxon_overlaps.py when a member KG is updated. UPDATE 2026-06-18: wildlifekn added as a LABEL-BRIDGED member - it has no NCBITaxon IRIs, so its bird/amphibian binomials (authority-stripped) are resolved to NCBITaxon via ubergraph rdfs:label (339 species resolve). Fragile vs the IRI-based members; exact-id pairwise overlaps verified 2026-06-18 (nde 17, sawgraph 2). UPDATE 2026-06-23: biohealth added as a LABEL-BRIDGED member - the Bio-Health KG keys every entity on a UMLS CUI (node IRI) and carries NO NCBITaxon ids, so its organism concepts are resolved to NCBITaxon by matching biohealth rdfs:label to ubergraph NCBITaxon rdfs:label (organism scientific name). Name-based and approximate (misses synonyms/spelling variants, so counts are conservative lower bounds) and CANNOT do subClassOf* clade expansion - even more fragile than wildlifekn (which at least uses cleaned binomials). Recorded as label_match counts (biohealth organisms found by name in each hub KG), NOT exact_id/clade, verified 2026-06-23: aopwiki 112/166, gene-expression-atlas-okn 6/8, sawgraph 377/538, spoke-genelab 7/9 (model organisms), nde 1052/1808, spoke-okn 1603/34570.

verified_crosswalks.overlap_with_doid_join: Checked against spoke-okn's established DOID disease join. spoke-okn has 180 biolink:Disease nodes, ALL of them DOID-identified (the node IRI is http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/DOID_{n}); mesh_list hangs the MeSH id directly on 159 of those same DOID nodes (155 distinct MeSH). So for DISEASES the MeSH route and the DOID route reach the SAME entities - MeSH is a co-located annotation on the DOID nodes, not a different slice (0 MeSH-tagged diseases are non-DOID; 21 DOID disease nodes simply carry no MeSH). M2's disease half therefore adds no new spoke-okn disease entities beyond the DOID join, but it DOES materialize a verified MeSH<->DOID correspondence on those 159 shared nodes (e.g. D015212<->DOID:0050589 inflammatory bowel disease, D000071243<->DOID:0060478 Zika fever), usable as a MeSH->DOID->MONDO bridge. The genuinely unique reach is the 10 SDoH nodes (mesh_ids), which are not Disease/DOID and have no MONDO term, so neither the DOID join nor M1 touches them.

cross_route_validation.question: Do spoke-okn's MeSH<->DOID disease pairs (M2) agree with ubergraph's independent MeSH->MONDO xrefs (M1), once DOID is bridged to MONDO via ubergraph?
cross_route_validation.method: Took all 164 spoke (DOID, MeSH) disease pairs; mapped DOID->MONDO via ubergraph oboInOwl:hasDbXref 'DOID:{n}' (ubergraph holds 11,866 distinct DOID xrefs, and all 164 spoke DOIDs map), then compared the 'MESH:{id}' xref(s) on that same MONDO to spoke's MeSH. GOTCHA: matching a BIND-constructed string directly against the stored xref TERM returned 0 (literal datatype mismatch); the comparison only works when both sides are reduced to bare strings via STR()+REPLACE and intersected - same class of bug as the http/https issue in M2 and the cross-graph FILTER gotcha in K1/methodology_note.
cross_route_validation.interpretation: 72% (118/164) exact two-route corroboration. 19.5% (32/164) are pairs where ubergraph carries NO MeSH on the mapped MONDO - so M2 ADDS MeSH coverage ubergraph lacks, not a conflict. Only 8.5% (14/164) are true disagreements, and label inspection shows these are SEMANTICALLY ADJACENT, not flat errors: (a) organism-vs-disease axis - spoke tags the disease node with the pathogen's MeSH while ubergraph uses the disease term (chlamydia: D002689 'Chlamydia' [genus] vs D002690 'Chlamydia Infections'; pertussis: D001885 'Bordetella Infections' vs D014917 'Whooping Cough'; also diphtheria, syphilis); and (b) parent/child or near-synonym granularity (depression D003863 'Depression' vs D003866 'Depressive Disorder'; squamous cell D018307 'Neoplasms, Squamous Cell' vs D002294 'Carcinoma, Squamous Cell'; nasopharynx D009303 'Nasopharyngeal Neoplasms' vs D000077274 'Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma'; tuberculosis D014375 'Tuberculoma' vs D014376 'Tuberculosis'; plus hepatitis, gout, uterine fibroid, generalized epilepsy, coronary artery disease, viral infectious disease).
cross_route_validation.upshot: MeSH is a HIGH- but not perfect-confidence bridge key. Exact-ID joins are trustworthy (72% corroborated by two independent routes, zero flat errors among the disagreements), but MeSH<->disease-ontology mappings are APPROXIMATE near the leaves - the main hazard is the organism-vs-disease axis (infections), where MeSH and DOID/MONDO legitimately pick different terms. For a high-precision federated join, prefer two-route corroboration (M1 & M2 agreeing) as a filter, and treat single-route MeSH leaf mappings for infectious diseases with care.

verified_crosswalks.key_namespace: http://id.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/{ID} (biobricks-mesh node IRI) ; "MESH:{ID}" string literal on oboInOwl:hasDbXref (ubergraph)
verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: biobricks-mesh entities ARE their own MeSH descriptor IRIs http://id.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/{ID} (e.g. .../D001249 = Asthma, .../D000086382 = COVID-19); extract the bare id REPLACE(STR(?s),'^http://id.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/',''). ubergraph carries MeSH cross-refs as oboInOwl:hasDbXref STRING LITERALS of the form 'MESH:{ID}' on OBO terms; strip the prefix REPLACE(STR(?x),'^MESH:',''). Join the two bare-id strings via two independent DISTINCT sub-SELECTs (one scoped to each named graph) and intersect on the shared ?id - a cross-graph FILTER(STR(?a)=?b) returns 0 (same gotcha recorded for K1 / methodology_note).
verified_crosswalks.hinge_note: THIS IS biobricks-mesh's attachment to the federation. biobricks-mesh is a standalone MeSH vocabulary keyed only by its own MeSH descriptor IRIs (it carries no outbound ontology xref of its own), so it reaches the federation through ubergraph, which cross-references 10,004 MeSH ids on OBO terms. 9,463 MeSH descriptors match - 8,202 of them MONDO disease terms - so via ubergraph's MONDO hub biobricks-mesh joins the entire disease cluster (A): oard-kg, rdkg, prokn and nde (which key disease on MONDO/HP) and spoke-okn (through the ubergraph DOID<->MONDO bridge, A10-A11). The match also reaches 1,051 UBERON anatomy and 83 CL cell-type terms. NOTE: MeSH chemical (D-category) descriptors pick up NO CHEBI xref on this predicate (0 CHEBI matches), so this is a disease/anatomy bridge, not a chemical one.

verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: Both graphs classify facilities/manufacturers with NAICS but mint the NAICS IRI differently. fiokg: the object of ofPrimaryIndustry/ofSecondaryIndustry is http://w3id.org/fio/v1/naics#NAICS-{6-digit} (extract the bare code REPLACE(STR(?ind),'^.*naics#NAICS-([0-9]+)$','$1')). sudokn: http://asu.edu/semantics/SUDOKN/NAICS%20{code}-individual (extract REPLACE(STR(?n),'^.*NAICS%20([0-9]+)-individual$','$1') - same as base-file I1). A direct IRI join returns 0; intersect the two bare numeric codes via two DISTINCT sub-SELECTs (one per named graph).
verified_crosswalks.hinge_note: fiokg attaches to the manufacturing cluster (I) on the bare NAICS code: 64 of sudokn's 66 distinct NAICS codes also appear among fiokg's 3,842 (near-complete containment of sudokn's manufacturing codes in fiokg's national, all-sector facility set). This puts fiokg in the same NAICS world as sudokn and securechainkg (base-file I1/I2). The join is at the industry-classification level, NOT on individual facility/company instances (fiokg facilities and sudokn manufacturers have unrelated IRIs).

verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: geoconnex carries county FIPS as the object of the GNIS county predicate, an https://geoconnex.us/ref/counties/{FIPS5} reference IRI. Extract the bare 5-digit FIPS: REPLACE(STR(?county),'^.*/counties/([0-9]{5}).*$','$1'). spatialkg counties are KWG administrativeRegion.USA.{FIPS5} node IRIs (constrain with 'a kwg:AdministrativeRegion_2', which DOES work on spatialkg, then REGEX the IRI for the trailing 5 digits). Intersect the two bare-FIPS strings via two DISTINCT sub-SELECTs (see methodology_note). NOTE this is a DIFFERENT key than the two recorded geoconnex non-joins (S2 Level-13 cells; SAWGraph PWS reference IRIs), both of which remain genuine non-joins.
verified_crosswalks.hinge_note: THIS IS geoconnex's attachment to the SAWGraph spatial hub. 3,114 of geoconnex's 3,243 distinct county FIPS match a spatialkg AdministrativeRegion_2 county (spatialkg covers the 48 contiguous states + DC; the unmatched ~129 are AK/HI/PR/territory counties spatialkg does not load). Via this key geoconnex's hydrologic features (wells, streams, monitoring sites - placed in a county by the GNIS county predicate) roll up to spatialkg's S2 grid and admin-region hierarchy, making geoconnex a county-keyed member of the SAWGraph spatial world alongside sockg, ruralkg and spoke-okn.

verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: Shared key NCBITaxon (obo/NCBITaxon_). spoke-genelab stores each gene's organism as a STRING literal holding the NCBITaxon IRI on the Gene.taxonomy node property (schema/taxonomy), NOT as a node — coerce it to an IRI with BIND(IRI(STR(?ts)) AS ?taxon) before joining ubergraph's taxonomy. All 9 distinct model-organism taxa (human 9606, mouse 10090, Arabidopsis 3702, C. elegans 6239, zebrafish 7955, Drosophila 7227, rat 10116, yeast 4932, Monodelphis domestica 13613) exist in ubergraph (9/9). For CATEGORY questions expand a clade inline via ?taxon rdfs:subClassOf* <parent NCBITaxon term> on ubergraph, then join to spoke-genelab. NOTE: this entry covers ONLY spoke-genelab's 9 model-organism taxa (Gene.taxonomy). spoke-genelab has a SECOND taxon representation — its microbiome Organism class (46 label-only genus/family NAMES e.g. 'Pseudomonas', no NCBITaxon id) — which does NOT join by id but IS reachable by resolving the name via ubergraph rdfs:label and expanding the clade; recorded as its OWN hub spoke D10 (spoke-genelab microbiome <-> ubergraph; the NCBI taxon id is embedded in the Organism node IRI .../node/{taxid}, all 46 resolve), and expanded to spoke-okn strains in D9 (33,313 shared taxa). So spoke-genelab's full taxon footprint in the hub is 9 model-organism ids (this entry) + 41 microbiome names (D10).
verified_crosswalks.verified_count_note: DISTINCT spoke-genelab Gene.taxonomy NCBITaxon terms present in ubergraph (9/9 = 100%). These are the model-organism taxa of the differential-expression genes; the join lets ubergraph's taxonomy lineage/clade closure be applied to spoke-genelab genes.

verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: Shared key NCBITaxon (obo/NCBITaxon_). spoke-okn does NOT carry obo/NCBITaxon_ IRIs directly: its biolink:OrganismTaxon nodes (321,442 bacterial strains + other organisms) are PATRIC/BV-BRC genome IRIs of the form .../spoke-okn/organism/{ncbi_taxon_id}.{assembly} (e.g. organism/100053.4). Extract the integer taxon-id prefix with REPLACE(STR(?o),'^.*/organism/([0-9]+).*$','$1') ([0-9]+ stops at the dot, no escaping) and rebuild obo/NCBITaxon_{id}, then join ubergraph. Collapse to DISTINCT taxa first (321k genome assemblies map to 34,570 distinct taxa) before probing ubergraph. For CATEGORY questions expand a clade inline via ?taxon rdfs:subClassOf* <parent NCBITaxon term> on ubergraph, then join to spoke-okn.
verified_crosswalks.verified_count_note: DISTINCT spoke-okn organism taxa (extracted from PATRIC genome IRIs) present in ubergraph's taxonomy: 33,602 of 34,570 (97.2%). The ~968 misses are mostly strain-level PATRIC taxon ids absent from ubergraph's NCBITaxon snapshot. Mostly bacterial pathogens; complements D3 (sawgraph) and D4 (spoke-genelab) on the same ubergraph taxonomy hub.

verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: Shared key NCBITaxon (obo/NCBITaxon_). nde stores each dataset's species as https://www.uniprot.org/taxonomy/{id} on schema:species; the UniProt taxonomy id IS the NCBI taxon id. Extract it with REPLACE(STR(?o),'^.*/taxonomy/([0-9]+).*$','$1') and rebuild obo/NCBITaxon_{id}, then join ubergraph. (The server normalizes https schema.org to http, so the predicate is http://schema.org/species.) 1,797 of 1,808 distinct species join ubergraph. Collapse to DISTINCT taxa first.

verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: spoke-genelab's microbiome organisms encode the NCBI taxon id in the node IRI (.../node/{ncbi_taxon_id}); extract it (parallel to spoke-okn's D5/D10) rather than resolving rdfs:label. Then bridge through ubergraph: expand each microbiome taxon's clade with ?desc rdfs:subClassOf* ?taxon and match spoke-okn's strain taxids (also extracted from .../organism/{id}.{n}). The join needs the ubergraph clade closure (spoke-genelab gives genus/family-level taxa, spoke-okn gives strains) so it cannot be done pairwise; the id route is robust to ubergraph label renames the old label join lost.
verified_crosswalks.verified_count_note: DISTINCT spoke-okn organism taxa nested under spoke-genelab's microbiome genus/family clades (33,313 of spoke-okn's 34,570 = 96%). High because spoke-genelab's microbiome includes broad groups (e.g. NCBITaxon_2 'Bacteria', Gammaproteobacteria) that cover most of spoke-okn's bacterial strains. The overlap an exact-id intersection misses: spoke-genelab and spoke-okn meet only via ubergraph's taxonomy closure.

verified_crosswalks.methodology_note: spoke-genelab carries taxa in TWO id forms: 9 model organisms as obo NCBITaxon IRIs on Gene.taxonomy (D4), and 46 microbiome taxa as NCBI taxon ids embedded in the Organism node IRI (D10, this entry's left side). The latter overlap spoke-okn massively but only via ubergraph clade expansion — an exact-id matrix reports a tiny count and is wrong for coarser-grained taxa.

verified_crosswalks.right_predicate: rdfs:label (NCBITaxon term), then subClassOf* for category expansion
verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: Companion to D4. spoke-genelab's microbiome organisms (the Organism class, 46 nodes) encode the NCBI taxon id DIRECTLY in the node IRI: .../spoke-genelab/node/{ncbi_taxon_id} (e.g. node/286 = Pseudomonas, node/2 = Bacteria, node/106589 = Cupriavidus) — they are NOT label-only. Extract the id with REPLACE(STR(?node),'^.*/node/([0-9]+).*$','$1') and rebuild obo/NCBITaxon_{id} (parallel to spoke-okn's D5), then confirm in ubergraph. ALL 46 resolve; the IRI route is more complete and robust than matching rdfs:label, which dropped 5 to ubergraph renames/synonyms (Actinobacteria->Actinomycetota, Eoetvoesia->Eoetvoesiella, the Burkholderia-Caballeronia-Paraburkholderia complex, two 'sp.' fungi). For category queries expand a clade via ?desc rdfs:subClassOf* ?taxon on ubergraph (this is what D9 does to reach spoke-okn).

verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: LABEL-BRIDGED join (fragile, verified 2026-06-18): wildlifekn stores species as scientific-name label strings WITH taxonomic authority (e.g. 'Ardea alba Linnaeus, 1758'); there are NO NCBITaxon IRIs. Strip the authority to the bare binomial (first two whitespace tokens) and resolve to an NCBITaxon IRI via ubergraph rdfs:label, then intersect with the partner KG's NCBITaxon set. Unlike the IRI-based taxonomy joins (D3-D10) this depends on exact binomial/label agreement and collapses subspecies to species rank; the verified_count is the EXACT-ID overlap. 339 of wildlifekn's bird/amphibian species resolve to an NCBITaxon term this way.

verified_crosswalks.key_namespace: bare county FIPS as a NUMERIC literal, leading zero dropped (scales) ; http://stko-kwg.geog.ucsb.edu/lod/resource/administrativeRegion.USA.{FIPS5} (spatialkg)
verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: CORRECTS the base-file verdict that scales is a geographic island: the curated 'fips:CountyCode' schema field IS unpopulated, but the SCALES IDB (Federal Judicial Center Integrated Data Base) field hasIdbCounty carries the genuine 5-digit county FIPS - stored as a NUMERIC literal (xsd:decimal/integer), so the leading zero is dropped (e.g. 6037.0 = California 06037 = Los Angeles County; 4013.0 = Arizona 04013 = Maricopa). Normalize: cast to integer then string (STR(xsd:integer(?county))), DROP the sentinel value '88888' (FJC 'unknown/out-of-US' code, the single most frequent value), then zero-pad any 4-digit result to 5 (IF(STRLEN(?ci)=4, CONCAT('0',?ci), ?ci)). Intersect this padded FIPS string against spatialkg's AdministrativeRegion_2 IRIs (REGEX trailing 5 digits).
verified_crosswalks.hinge_note: THIS IS scales's attachment to the SAWGraph spatial hub, and a correction to its base-file island status. scales holds 3,129 distinct valid county FIPS on hasIdbCounty (near-complete national coverage of federal court cases by county of filing); 3,029 of them match a spatialkg county (the ~100 unmatched are AK/HI/PR/territory + the 88888 sentinel). Via this key federal criminal/civil court activity (charges, parties, dispositions) rolls up to the county and joins the SAWGraph spatial world - and meets ruralkg's rural health+justice indicators (base-file K2) on the same county key.

verified_crosswalks.key_namespace: FBI NIBRS/UCR offense-category NAME as a plain string literal, identical on both sides (e.g. 'Aggravated Assault', 'Drug/Narcotic Violations', 'Robbery'). scales attaches it to jxdm:Charge nodes via fbi:OffenseUCRCode; ruralkg attaches it to NIBRSAnswer nodes via variable/answerContent (which also carry the matching NIBRS variable/answerCode, e.g. 131 = Aggravated Assault, 351 = Drug/Narcotic Violations). Both sides ingest the FBI NIBRS crime taxonomy, so this is a CONTROLLED-vocabulary match, not fuzzy label collision.
verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: NEW join enabled by the 2026-07-01 scales entities.csv update, which added the populated fbi:OffenseUCRCode predicate (2,689,214 charge triples; the sibling niem fips:CountyCode, LocaleCensusBlockID and postal-code predicates were added to the schema but carry 0 triples). Join directly on the shared string literal by binding the SAME variable in both GRAPH blocks (GRAPH scales { ?ch fbi:OffenseUCRCode ?off } GRAPH ruralkg { ?ans rk:answerContent ?off }). Do NOT join with a cross-graph FILTER(STR(?a)=STR(?b)) equality — the federation engine mishandles that theta-join and silently returns 0 even though exact matches exist. Match is exact/case-sensitive; a few scales offense strings differ only in case or wording from ruralkg's ('ASSAULT OFFENSES' vs 'Assault Offenses') and legitimately do not join.
verified_crosswalks.hinge_note: scales's attachment to ruralkg on the OFFENSE-TYPE axis — complementary to, and independent of, the county-FIPS axis on which scales already meets spatialkg (L4) and spoke-okn (L5). 37 distinct NIBRS offense categories are shared: scales supplies real federal-court charge VOLUME per offense (e.g. Drug/Narcotic Violations 86,454 charges; Simple Assault 177,758; Aggravated Assault 34,298), ruralkg supplies the rural crime-reporting CODEBOOK — the NIBRS answer codes and the survey variables (165 of them, e.g. 'UCR ARREST OFFENSE CODE') that instrument each offense. This is a CATEGORICAL join (37 offense categories), not an entity-level identity join: use it to compare federal charge activity by offense type against ruralkg's rural crime-data instrumentation, not to link individual cases.

verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: Both graphs classify manufacturers with the SAME predicate (SUDOKN:hasPrimaryNAICSClassifier) but mint the NAICS classifier IRI differently. securechainkg: 'http://asu.edu/semantics/SUDOKN/naics-311111.0-inst' (lowercase 'naics-', a trailing '.0', suffix '-inst'). sudokn: 'http://asu.edu/semantics/SUDOKN/NAICS%20332710-individual' (uppercase 'NAICS', %20 space, suffix '-individual'). A direct IRI join returns 0; extract the bare numeric code from each and join on it: securechainkg REPLACE(STR(?n),'^.*/naics-([0-9]+)\\.0-inst$','$1'); sudokn REPLACE(STR(?n),'^.*/NAICS%20([0-9]+)-individual$','$1').
verified_crosswalks.hinge_note: The two KGs do NOT share manufacturer/company instance IRIs (securechainkg mints '...{name}-company-inst' from DHS/D&B/MSKG sources; sudokn mints '...{domain}-company-instance'); a direct company join is 0. They join on the industry-classification keys, not on individual firms. 35 of sudokn's 66 NAICS codes are also used in securechainkg (which spans 301 codes total).

verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: suppliesToIndustry targets a small shared SUDOKN industry-sector controlled vocabulary, again minted differently per graph. securechainkg: 'http://asu.edu/semantics/SUDOKN/renewableenergy-inst' (lowercase, no spaces, '-inst'). sudokn: 'http://asu.edu/semantics/SUDOKN/Renewable%20Energy-industry-individual' (Title Case, %20 spaces, '-industry-individual'). Direct IRI join is 0. Normalize each to a lowercase, space-free label and join on it: securechainkg LCASE(REPLACE(REPLACE(STR(?ind),'^.*/',''),'-inst$','')); sudokn LCASE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(STR(?ind),'^.*/',''),'-industry-individual$',''),'%20','')).

verified_crosswalks.hinge_note: sockg is a THIRD spatial leaf on the SAWGraph S2 hub, alongside sawgraph (Maine PFAS, D2) and hydrologykg (Illinois wells/streams, D1). It materializes its S2 Level-13 cells as its own typed nodes in the identical KWG resource IRI form (http://stko-kwg.geog.ucsb.edu/lod/resource/s2.level13.{id}), so the join to spatialkg's S2Cell_Level13 nodes is direct, no rewrite. All 1069 sockg S2 cells are present in spatialkg. Soil-carbon experiment sites are multi-state; this leaf joins to the national hub here, but it DOES additionally co-locate leaf-to-leaf with sawgraph in 2 cells via sawgraph's national US-WQP layer (see H3-s2-sockg-sawgraph) - an earlier version of this note wrongly stated it does not co-locate with the other leaves, which assumed sawgraph = Maine only.

verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: DIRECT leaf-to-leaf join, no rewrite: sockg materializes its S2 Level-13 cells as its own typed nodes (a kwg:S2Cell_Level13) in the KWG resource form http://stko-kwg.geog.ucsb.edu/lod/resource/s2.level13.{id}; sawgraph carries the IDENTICAL cell IRI as an owl:sameAs object on its sample/feature nodes (base-file D2). Bind sawgraph's owl:sameAs object and reuse the SAME variable as sockg's typed cell subject. GOTCHA: requiring 'a kwg:S2Cell_Level13' on BOTH sides returns 0 - sawgraph types these particular shared cells only as geo:SpatialObject/owl:Thing (not S2Cell_Level13), so scope the type on the SOCKG side only and match sawgraph on the raw cell IRI (owl:sameAs object, or kwg:sfContains).
verified_crosswalks.hinge_note: A genuine DIRECT leaf-to-leaf spatial join (most SAWGraph S2 leaves only meet THROUGH the spatialkg hub). Exactly 2 S2 Level-13 cells carry BOTH a sockg soil-organic-carbon experiment Location (USDA REAP sites Location.MNMOONFM in Minnesota and Location.ALAUTVS in Alabama, both rdfs:label 'REAP') and a sawgraph contaminant sample point. The overlap comes from sawgraph's NATIONAL US-WQP (Water Quality Portal) layer, not its Maine PFAS core - so soil-carbon experiment sites co-locate with PFAS water-monitoring samples. In both cells the co-located US-WQP sample was screened for ~22 PFAS analytes and returned non-detect, so this is a PFAS-screening co-location (a clean agricultural site) rather than a contamination hotspot. Small but real: it turns an agronomy KG and a contaminant KG into a soil-management-vs-PFAS-exposure question in the same ~1 km cell. For everything else, both roll up to the national hub via H1/D2.

verified_crosswalks.left_predicate: https://schema.org/value (literal object of a blank node typed both schema:PropertyValue and kwg:S2Cell, carrying schema:name 's2Level13')
verified_crosswalks.key_namespace: http://stko-kwg.geog.ucsb.edu/lod/resource/s2.level13.{id} (spatialkg node IRI) ; bare decimal 64-bit S2 cell id as a string literal (ufokn schema:value)
verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: ufokn does NOT materialize its S2 cells as KWG resource IRIs - they are BLANK NODES typed both schema:PropertyValue and <https://stko-kwg.geog.ucsb.edu/lod/ontology#S2Cell> (note: https + /lod/ontology#, the ufokn ontology IRI, which is NOT spatialkg's <http://stko-kwg.geog.ucsb.edu/lod/ontology/S2Cell_Level13> node-type IRI). Each blank node carries schema:name ('s2Level13' or 's2Level18'), schema:description ('S2 cell at level 13'/'...18') and schema:value = the cell's 64-bit S2 id as a DECIMAL STRING (e.g. '9813806808853118976'). spatialkg materializes the SAME decimal id as the suffix of its S2Cell_Level13 node IRI http://stko-kwg.geog.ucsb.edu/lod/resource/s2.level13.{id} (base-file D1/D2/H1/N1), so the join is DIRECT with NO value rewrite: extract ufokn's schema:value, BIND(IRI(CONCAT('http://stko-kwg.geog.ucsb.edu/lod/resource/s2.level13.', STR(?val))) AS ?cell), and reuse ?cell as the subject in the spatialkg GRAPH block ('?cell a kwg:S2Cell_Level13'). The BIND-injected IRI DOES push down into the spatialkg block (verified). TWO OKN GOTCHAS make the ufokn side unqueryable the naive way and are why the base file scored this 0/unprofiled: (1) CONSTANT-PREDICATE / schema.org-https: a bound constant predicate on these nodes silently returns 0 - '?cell <https://schema.org/value> ?v' yields nothing even though '?cell ?p ?v' returns ?p = https://schema.org/value with the value. ufokn stores schema:value under the https form, and the server canonicalizes a bracketed <https://schema.org/value> to http, so read the value via a variable predicate and match it scheme-free - FILTER(STRENDS(STR(?p),'schema.org/value')) - or exactly: FILTER(?p = IRI(CONCAT('https://schema.org/','value'))) (the server preserves the https string literal inside IRI(CONCAT), rewriting only bracketed IRIs). Cheaper still, skip the predicate test and FILTER the object by shape: isLiteral && REGEX(STR(?val),'^[0-9]{18,20}$'). (2) LARGE-GRAPH: ufokn has ~11.7M S2Cell-typed nodes; any unbounded DISTINCT/FILTER scan times out at 120s. Scope the ufokn side in an inner sub-SELECT '{ SELECT ?cell WHERE { GRAPH ufokn { ?cell a kwg:S2Cell } } LIMIT N }', THEN pull '?cell ?p ?val' with the regex object-filter, THEN rebuild and join to the light spatialkg side. Level-18 values harmlessly do not match (they are not level-13 ids), so no name-filter is required for correctness - feed all schema:value objects and the intersection is exactly the level-13 overlap.
verified_crosswalks.verified_count_note: EXACT full level-13 join, re-derived via skeleton_query over all ufokn s2Level13 PropertyValue nodes (no sampling). Because ufokn's coverage is the continental US, it co-occupies cells with the national leaf fiokg broadly and with the Maine/Illinois leaves within those states; like the other leaves it meets them through the hub (D1/H1 pattern), and a direct leaf-to-leaf join was NOT separately verified here (regional sampling makes a leaf-to-leaf count unreliable - assert it only via the hub). verified_crosswalks.left_predicate: rdfs:seeAlso (Ensembl gene id, stored as a STRING LITERAL)
verified_crosswalks.key_namespace: https://www.ensembl.org/id/ENSG{n} - pankgraph stores it as a string LITERAL on rdfs:seeAlso; prokn uses the IRI form
verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: CRITICAL: pankgraph stores all its cross-references (Ensembl, GO, dbSNP) as STRING LITERALS on rdfs:seeAlso, NOT as IRIs. A naive cross-graph variable join therefore returns 0 (literal != IRI), even though both graphs hold the same gene. Convert with BIND(IRI(STR(?lit))) and drive from pankgraph: ?g rdfs:seeAlso ?lit (FILTER STRSTARTS https://www.ensembl.org/id/ENSG), BIND(IRI(STR(?lit)) AS ?ens), then match prokn's Ensembl gene node ?ens. prokn's Ensembl node carries MSigDB pathways (RO_0002431), UBERON tissue expression (RO_0002206), the encoded UniProt protein (SIO_010078) and HGNC (skos:exactMatch).
verified_crosswalks.verified_count_note: 37,835 of pankgraph's ~78,687 Ensembl genes are present in prokn (after literal->IRI conversion). Verified 2026-06-27. Attaches pankgraph (PanKbase islet KG) to the gene cluster on Ensembl, giving its islet genes ProKN's pathway/GO/protein/drug-target annotation. The naive join silently returns 0 because pankgraph stores Ensembl as a literal - see iri_normalization.

verified_crosswalks.right_predicate: obo:RO_0000056 object (protein -> Reactome pathway it is part of); the pathway node carries rdfs:label
verified_crosswalks.key_namespace: R-HSA-{n} - GXA stores it as https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-{n}; ProKN as https://identifiers.org/reactome/R-HSA-{n}. Extract the R-HSA accession and rebuild the identifiers.org form.
verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: GXA gene-set enrichment links a differential-expression contrast (assay, which has_attribute an EFO disease/tissue) to a Reactome pathway via a biolink:Association (enrichment_source='GXA:Reactome', biolink:object = https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-{n}, with adj_p_value). ProKN links proteins to Reactome pathways via obo:RO_0000056 (object = https://identifiers.org/reactome/R-HSA-{n}, pathway rdfs:label present). Normalize: BIND(IRI(CONCAT('https://identifiers.org/reactome/',REPLACE(STR(?gxaReact),'^.*/detail/','')))) then match ProKN. GXA also carries R-MMU (mouse) Reactome ids - filter to R-HSA for human.
verified_crosswalks.verified_count_note: 1,068 Reactome pathways shared between GXA (differential-expression enrichment) and ProKN (protein pathway membership). Verified 2026-06-27. Complementary halves: GXA says WHICH pathways are differentially active in a disease/perturbation (with adj p), ProKN says WHICH proteins constitute the pathway. Join e.g. colon adenocarcinoma -> 'Resolution of Sister Chromatid Cohesion' (GXA adj p 3e-12) -> 127 ProKN proteins (NDC80, BIRC5/Survivin, KIF2A...). First Pathways axis in the federation.

verified_crosswalks.methodology_note: Pathways axis. ProKN is the federation's pathway hub: Reactome (RO_0000056, joins GXA here), plus MSigDB (RO_0002431) and WikiPathways - the latter two are ProKN-internal IRIs with no second KG, so no crosswalk. Each carries hundreds of ToxCast assay endpoints (e.g. GenX/HFPO-DA, CAS 13252-13-6, has 506 endpoints and 2,184 SAWGraph water-sample observations). verified_crosswalks.key_namespace: sawgraph coso:casNumber (undashed OR dashed literal; dashes must be reconstructed) -> http://identifiers.org/cas/{cas} (biobricks-ice edam:has_identifier IRI)
verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: CORRECTED 2026-07-12 - THE PREVIOUS RECIPE UNDERCOUNTED BY 3x. SAWGraph's coso:casNumber is NOT reliably dashed: of its 131 distinct CAS values only 38 are dashed, 78 are UNDASHED digit strings ('120226600'), and 15 are non-CAS lab codes ('DEP14447'). The old skeleton filtered REGEX '^[0-9]+-[0-9]+-[0-9]$', so it silently saw only the dashed 38 and reported 12 shared. RECONSTRUCT the dashes before building the IRI: match undashed with FILTER(REGEX(STR(?raw),'^[0-9]{5,10}$')) and BIND(REPLACE(STR(?raw),'^([0-9]+)([0-9]{2})([0-9])$','$1-$2-$3')), keep already-dashed values as-is, then BIND(IRI(CONCAT('http://identifiers.org/cas/', ?cas))) and INNER-join ICE (the OPTIONAL pattern returns a false 0). ICE entities also carry a DSSTox DTXSID and rdfs:label.
verified_crosswalks.verified_count_note: 39 of SAWGraph's 116 well-formed CAS contaminants have biobricks-ICE (EPA Integrated Chemical Environment) records. Re-verified 2026-07-12 after fixing the undashed-literal normalization; the previous count of 12 was an artifact of a dashed-only regex that ignored 78 of SAWGraph's 131 CAS values. ICE resolves each environmental contaminant to its EPA CompTox identity (DTXSID + standardized name + functional-use categorization).

verified_crosswalks.methodology_note: DSSTox is NOT a useful second axis for this pair. SAWGraph exposes coso:ofDSSToxSubstance (86 distinct DTXSIDs) and ICE/ToxCast expose DTXSID on edam:has_identifier, but the DSSTox join reaches only 35 ICE chemicals - FEWER than the 39 a correctly-normalized CAS join reaches. Of SAWGraph's 86 DSSTox substances, 80 have a CAS and the 6 without one join to ICE ZERO times. DSSTox's single unique hit (DTXSID7022546) is a SAWGraph data-quality bug: its source node is parameter.PFECHS_A (a PFAS) but it is labelled 'Acetohydroxamic acid'. Use CAS; do not add a DSSTox edge. Verified 2026-07-12.

verified_crosswalks.left_predicate: schema:audienceType (target population of a social service: a health condition or social determinant, as a lowercase string LITERAL)
verified_crosswalks.shared_key: concept label (social-service audience term <-> UMLS concept name)
verified_crosswalks.key_namespace: dreamkg schema:audienceType free-text term (e.g. 'anxiety', 'veterans', 'uninsured') <-> biohealth rdfs:label (UMLS concept name, Title-case)
verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: dreamkg stores its service target audiences as informal lowercase string literals on schema:audienceType (81 distinct: a mix of health conditions - anxiety, bipolar, depression, ptsd, hiv/aids, eating disorder, opioid/alcohol dependency, covid19 - and social determinants - homeless, low-income, uninsured, unemployed, veterans, immigrants, refugees). biohealth uses Title-case UMLS concept names. Match by capitalizing the dreamkg term: BIND(CONCAT(UCASE(SUBSTR(?aud,1,1)),SUBSTR(?aud,2))) and INNER-join biohealth rdfs:label (the OPTIONAL pattern returns a false 0). Some terms need light curated expansion ('bipolar'->'Bipolar Disorder', 'homeless'->'Homelessness', 'eating disorder'->'Eating Disorders', 'hiv/aids'->'HIV').
verified_crosswalks.verified_count_note: 14 dreamkg audience terms exact-match a biohealth concept with only first-letter capitalization (Anxiety, Bipolar, Employed, Female, Immigrants, Mothers, Refugees, Retirement, Runaways, Substance, Teens, Underinsured, Uninsured, Veterans); a further ~10 match with light curated normalization (Depression, Bipolar Disorder, Eating Disorders, HIV, Suicide, Homelessness, Unemployment, Domestic Violence, Developmental Disabilities, Chronic disease) - ~24 of 81 total. Verified 2026-06-27. First CROSS-DOMAIN bridge from the social-services / homelessness domain (DREAM-KG, Philadelphia AuntBertha food/shelter/mental-health services) into health: it links 'what social services exist for population X' to biohealth's clinical+SDoH knowledge of X.
verified_crosswalks.complementary_note: Conceptually adjacent to the SDoH cluster (BH18 spoke-okn SDoH <-> biohealth): dreamkg's social-determinant audiences (homeless, uninsured, unemployed, veterans) overlap that SDoH vocabulary, while its clinical audiences (anxiety, bipolar, hiv/aids) reach biohealth's disease concepts.

verified_crosswalks.left_predicate: rdfs:label (OBO class label of a PHASES / BCIO psychosocial term, e.g. 'social isolation behavior disposition')
verified_crosswalks.shared_key: concept label (psychosocial / SDoH term <-> UMLS concept name)
verified_crosswalks.key_namespace: phaseskg rdfs:label (OBO class label) <-> biohealth rdfs:label (UMLS concept name, Title-case). Curated 8-concept equivalence on the social-connection / aging axis.
verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: phaseskg is an OBO/BFO T-Box ontology; its native PHASES_ / BCIO_ class labels carry qualifier suffixes ('... disposition', '... process', '... behavior disposition', '... representational pattern quality') that biohealth's bare UMLS concept names lack, so a raw label join fails. Match on the core concept (strip the suffix; case-insensitive; normalize the self-efficacy hyphen), giving a curated 8-pair equivalence to biohealth UMLS-CUI nodes. hasDbXref is NOT usable (phaseskg carries only 4 xrefs, all on imported upper-ontology terms, to Wikipedia/Wikidata/GOC) and the domain terms carry no external identifier - the label is the only bridge.
verified_crosswalks.verified_count_note: 8 phaseskg psychosocial concepts label-match a connected biohealth UMLS concept (biohealth out-degree in parens): feeling of loneliness -> C0023974 Loneliness (419); self-efficacy representational pattern quality -> C0600564 Self Efficacy (406); social withdrawal disposition -> C0424095 Social withdrawal (112); reminiscence therapy process -> C0150321 Reminiscence therapy (80); social alienation -> C0870124 Alienation (70, approximate); shyness behavior disposition -> C0037020 Shyness (9); social isolation behavior disposition -> C0037421 Social isolation (9); social detachment disposition -> C0700137 Social detachment (4). Curated lower bound. Verified 2026-07-11.
verified_crosswalks.complementary_note: Third biohealth label bridge into the SDoH / psychosocial layer, alongside SS1 (dreamkg social-service audiences) and BH18 (spoke-okn SDoH). phaseskg contributes the healthy-aging / loneliness ontology vocabulary; these concepts are social determinants, not diseases, so they stay in biohealth's SDoH / psychosocial layer (biohealth's UMLS->MONDO/DOID route is disease-only and does not carry them onward).

verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: NODE-IRI JOIN, no rewrite: hydrologykg does not merely reference COMIDs, it mints its reach subjects as geoconnex's own https://geoconnex.us/nhdplusv2/comid/{id} IRIs, so geoconnex's wd:P885/P403 objects match hydrologykg subjects directly. Confirmed two independent ways (direct IRI match, and local-id extraction intersected with the nhdplusv2:hasCOMID literal) - both return exactly 11,392. GOTCHAS: (1) geoconnex's schema.org predicates are stored with the HTTPS scheme, and the endpoint canonicalizes a bracketed <https://schema.org/...> to http, so a bracketed schema.org IRI matches NOTHING - use BIND(IRI(CONCAT('https://schema.org/','head_nhdpv1_comid'))) (the STRENDS form works but times out on an unbounded scan). (2) Do NOT put the head/outlet UNION inside a single GRAPH block with bound predicate vars - the planner explodes (tried to allocate 210 GB); UNION two SELECT DISTINCT sub-queries OUTSIDE the GRAPH blocks. (3) v1-vs-v2 is a naming misnomer, not a value-space difference: geoconnex's 'head_nhdpv1_comid' literal and its wd:P885 NHDPlus-v2 COMID IRI carry the same id (verified on mainstem 356782 -> 10079250), so treat nhdpv1_comid as a v2 COMID. (4) COMID is an xsd:string on BOTH sides - bind the same variable, never a cross-graph FILTER(STR(?a)=STR(?b)).
verified_crosswalks.verified_count_note: 11,392 shared NHDPlus reaches on the node-IRI route (geoconnex 67,734 distinct COMID IRIs; hydrologykg 507,486 distinct COMIDs). Verified 2026-07-12, surfaced by the entities.csv refresh that exposed geoconnex's head/outlet comid predicates and hydrologykg's nhdplusv2:hasCOMID. The literal route (geoconnex's head/outlet_nhdpv1_comid literals x nhdplusv2:hasCOMID) reaches only 6,830 and is a STRICT SUBSET - only some mainstems carry the literals, while nearly all carry the P885/P403 COMID IRIs, so prefer the node-IRI route. ReachCode is NOT a usable second key: geoconnex has no reach-code predicate (its head_rf1id/outlet_rf1id are RF1 ids, a different scheme).

verified_crosswalks.methodology_note: SUPERSEDES the M1 recipe's statement that biobricks-mesh is 'a disease/anatomy bridge, not a chemical one' (which was based on MeSH carrying 0 CHEBI xrefs). MeSH DOES have an outbound chemical xref - it is CAS on registryNumber, not an OBO id. This de-islands biobricks-mesh into the CAS chemical cluster (M3-M7), where previously it reached the federation only through disease/anatomy (ubergraph MONDO/UBERON M1, spoke-okn DOID M2). STRUCTURAL CAVEAT: CAS sits on mesh:Concept nodes whose parent record (via ^mesh:preferredConcept) is usually an SCR_Chemical (mesh/C######), not a D-descriptor - so only 299 of the 6,924 shared ICE chemicals reach a mesh:pharmacologicalAction. The broader payoff is MeSH indexing (preferredMappedTo descriptor+qualifier pairs, synonymy), which makes a tox-assay CAS literature-retrievable in PubMed and, via M1, traceable toward MONDO disease terms. Modern MeSH puts the UNII in registryNumber when one exists, so some famous chemicals (2,4-D 94-75-7, formaldehyde 50-00-0) are absent from the CAS side entirely - a UNII crosswalk would be the way to recover them.

verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: THE ADVERTISED #fips FIELD IS A TRAP - DO NOT USE IT. climatemodelskg's #fips is a 2-letter FIPS 10-4 COUNTRY code (FI, DA, IZ), attached to cm:Country only; joined against spatialkg:hasFIPS or spoke-okn state FIPS it returns 0. Its #equivalent_fips_code is an EMPTY column (2 distinct values, sample ''). The county key is LATENT and COMPOSITE: assemble it from admin1_code (GeoNames admin1, which for the US is USPS LETTERS 'CA', not a numeric state FIPS) + admin2_code (the 3-digit county FIPS suffix '075'). spatialkg CANNOT decode 'CA'->'06' (its state nodes carry only hasFIPS and rdfs:label, no abbreviation), so spoke-okn is a MANDATORY BRIDGE: its state node IRI .../location/06 carries spoke:abbr 'CA'. Extract the state FIPS from that IRI's local name (REPLACE(STR(?st),'^.*/location/','')) and CONCAT with admin2_code. LEADING ZEROS ARE ALREADY CORRECT AND MUST BE PRESERVED - admin2_code is a STRING '067' and the spoke-okn local name is '06', so CONCAT yields a clean '06075'; do NOT cast to integer anywhere (this KG dodges the scales leading-zero bug). Filter cm:country_code 'US' first - admin2_code is populated for all 30,062 world cities but is only a county FIPS for the US.

verified_crosswalks.iri_normalization: SCHEME TRAP: ruralkg stores https://schema.org/postalCode, and the endpoint canonicalizes a BRACKETED <https://...> to http - so a bracketed IRI matches NOTHING. cluster_notes.A_disease: spoke-okn keys diseases on DOID (180 biolink:Disease nodes whose IRI is the obo/DOID_ term). It joins the DOID carriers DIRECTLY on the shared DOID IRI: prokn 96 (A7), biomarkerkg 79 (A8), nde 20 (A9; nde's schema:healthCondition holds DOID alongside MONDO/HP/NCIT). The MONDO-keyed members need a DOID->MONDO bridge through ubergraph (?mondo skos:exactMatch ?doid, equivalently oboInOwl:hasDbXref 'DOID:{id}' - both give identical coverage): rdkg 149 (A10, the broadest spoke-okn disease join since rdkg is rare-disease-rich), oard-kg 40 (A11, attaching spoke-okn to the disease-cluster hub; the existing DOID pair biomarkerkg<->prokn is A5). Every federation disease KG is thus reachable from spoke-okn: DOID carriers directly, MONDO members via ubergraph. Caveat: spoke-okn's disease set is small (180), so counts are bounded by spoke-okn.
cluster_notes.C_gene_cluster: The gene cluster spans THREE id systems. (1) ENTREZ / NCBI Gene is the federation's de-facto gene join key, but in THREE IRI FORMS: http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/{id} (spoke-okn and spoke-genelab gene NODES; spoke-okn types them biolink:Gene, 16,346 nodes), http://identifiers.org/ncbigene/{id} (rdkg gene nodes), and https://identifiers.org/ncbigene/{id} (biobricks-aopwiki, as skos:exactMatch on key-event target genes). Same numeric id - join by stripping to the bare integer and rebuilding the partner's form (bind the same term in both GRAPH blocks; never FILTER(STR(?a)=?b), which returns 0 here). Verified Entrez pairs: spoke-okn<->spoke-genelab (C4, 16,326), rdkg<->spoke-okn (C5, 8,475), rdkg<->spoke-genelab (C6, 9,034), aopwiki<->spoke-genelab (C7, 1,472), aopwiki<->rdkg (C8, 1,193). C7 is notable: spoke-genelab is Entrez-only, so AOP-Wiki - previously tied to the cluster only on Ensembl (F1/F2) - reaches it only via this Entrez route. (2) ENSEMBL members are gene-expression-atlas-okn, pankgraph and biobricks-aopwiki, plus spoke-okn via its schema/ensembl crosswalk (16,316 of its 16,346 genes carry an http://identifiers.org/ensembl/{ENSG} value). pankgraph is Ensembl-ONLY (its gene nodes are ensembl IRIs with no Entrez xref; only expressed_in->CL and functional_association->GO edges). The C1-C3/F1 joins to spoke-okn remain valid and unchanged, but the spoke-okn side is reached via the schema/ensembl predicate (Ensembl as object), not the gene node. (3) HGNC is carried ONLY by prokn (http://identifiers.org/hgnc/{N}, ~38,328 distinct ids, mostly on rdf:subject/rdf:object reified INDRA statements and rdfs:seeAlso). prokn has no Entrez/Ensembl of its own, so it bridges to the Entrez world through the WIKIDATA graph: HGNC bare id -> wdt:P354 -> same item's wdt:P351 (Entrez literal) -> rebuild the spoke Entrez IRI (C9: prokn<->spoke-okn 16,298, prokn<->spoke-genelab 27,226; ~99% of prokn HGNC ids resolve via P354). Note identifier-mappings does NOT carry HGNC - wikidata is the bridge. prokn is also a protein-cluster member (G1/G2, UniProt): it holds marker genes as HGNC and proteins as UniProt. HINGES: spoke-okn ties the Entrez and Ensembl sub-worlds together (it alone carries both - Entrez node + Ensembl crosswalk); wikidata ties HGNC to Entrez. So every gene member is reachable from every other: the Entrez core (spoke-okn, spoke-genelab, rdkg, aopwiki) directly, the Ensembl members (GXA, pankgraph) via spoke-okn's crosswalk, and prokn (HGNC) via wikidata.
cluster_notes.E_toxicology_cas: biobricks-tox21 and biobricks-aopwiki both attach to the CAS chemical cluster anchored by biobricks-toxcast / biobricks-ice (base file B1). tox21 joins natively (same http://identifiers.org/cas/ node-IRI form); AOP-Wiki needs the https->http rewrite. This makes AOP-Wiki a hinge: its stressors carry CAS (chemical cluster) AND its key-event targets carry Ensembl + UniProt (gene/protein clusters).
cluster_notes.F_aopwiki_gene_bridge: AOP-Wiki's skos:exactMatch block carries genes as BOTH Entrez (~1,480 https://identifiers.org/ncbigene/ ids) and Ensembl (~1,478 https://identifiers.org/ensembl/ENSG ids), plus hmdb/chebi/pubchem.compound/drugbank chemical ids. F1/F2 use its Ensembl route (to spoke-okn and GXA); the Entrez route is now verified too and links the Entrez-only member spoke-genelab (C7) and rdkg (C8). Standard https->http (or bare-id rebuild) normalization applies.
cluster_notes.G_protein_cluster: UniProt accession is a federation-wide protein key but appears in at least three IRI forms: http://identifiers.org/uniprot/ (ncipidkg), https://identifiers.org/uniprot/ (aopwiki), and http://purl.uniprot.org/uniprot/ (prokn, which models proteins with the UniProt core ontology). Always join on the bare accession, never the raw IRI.
cluster_notes.H_soil_spatial: sockg (Soil Organic Carbon KG) joins the SAWGraph spatial hub (base D-series) as a third leaf next to sawgraph (Maine PFAS) and hydrologykg (Illinois). It reuses the SAWGraph/KWG spatial stack wholesale: S2Cell_Level13 cells, GADM AdministrativeRegion_0..2 nodes, kwg:sfWithin / sfContains, spatial-full:connectedTo, and GeoSPARQL geometries — all in native KWG IRI forms, so attachment to spatialkg needs no rewrite. Note: sockg ALSO carries contaminoso:casNumber (coso/contaminoso vocabulary) on its chemical entities, the same CAS chemical world as base-file B1 (toxcast/ice) and the E-series — a real thread into the chemical cluster that is intentionally NOT expanded here (out of scope: chemical/tox is already covered).
cluster_notes.I_manufacturing_supply_chain: securechainkg embeds the SUDOKN manufacturing ontology (http://asu.edu/semantics/SUDOKN/*) almost in full on its Manufacturer entities: hasPrimaryNAICSClassifier, suppliesToIndustry, hasProcessCapability, hasMaterialCapability, organizationLocatedIn, hasCertificate, hasNumberOfEmployees, hasOrganizationYearOfEstablishment. This makes SecureChain and SUDOKN siblings on the manufacturing side. They share the industry-classification vocabularies (NAICS codes I1; industry sectors I2) but NOT the individual company instances (different IRI minting), so joins are at the industry-class level. Beyond the manufacturing overlap, securechainkg adds a software-supply-chain layer with no cross-KG partner in the federation: Software / SoftwareVersion / Vulnerability (CVE-style ids via schema:identifier), Hardware / HardwareVersion (CPE 2.3 via secure-chain:cpe23), license (schema:license) and dependsOn / vulnerableTo edges. These are useful securechainkg-internal join keys but have no second graph to bridge to here.
cluster_notes.J_spoke_okn_zip_geography: spoke-okn carries ~42,724 ZIP nodes (.../location/{STATE}-{ZIP}), ALL with a bare-ZIP rdfs:label (xsd:string) - the clean cross-KG key. (Only 978 also have a KWG ZipCodeArea rdfs:seeAlso, stored as an HTML-anchor literal and unusable as an IRI; do not gate on it - that was the bug that undercounted the first version of this file.) Partners with bare 5-digit ZIPs join directly: sudokn (hasZipcodeValue, 12,329), ruralkg (schema:postalCode, 4,938 = all of ruralkg), dreamkg (schema:postalCode, 53 = all of dreamkg). For coarser geography spoke-okn also exposes county FIPS and state FIPS in its node IRIs - see the admin-region file (cluster K), including its attachment to the spatialkg hub. Pervasive failure mode: the OKN cross-graph literal-join quirk (FILTER(STR(?a)=?b) yields 0; bind the same variable term in both GRAPH blocks).
cluster_notes.K_spoke_okn_admin_region_fips: spoke-okn's geographic hierarchy is fully FIPS-coded above the ZIP level, with the code living in the node-IRI suffix (.../location/{FIPS5} for counties, .../location/{FIPS2} for states) rather than in any KWG/identifiers.org IRI. Because the SAWGraph spatial stack (spatialkg hub; sockg and the sawgraph/hydrologykg leaves; ruralkg's censusCounty) keys admin regions on KWG administrativeRegion.USA.{FIPS}, the join is: extract the bare FIPS from spoke-okn -> rebuild the KWG IRI -> match as a shared-variable term. County FIPS is the strongest spoke-okn geographic key in the federation (national, 3,196 counties): spatialkg 3,122 (= spoke-okn's attachment to the hub), ruralkg 3,196 (full containment), sockg 31. State FIPS adds a coarse rollup (spatialkg 51, sockg 18). IMPORTANT CORRECTIONS to the prior files: (1) the earlier 'spoke-okn <-> spatialkg = 0 / no hub attachment' non-join was a ZIP-level result only; via county/state FIPS spoke-okn DOES attach to the hub (K1, K4). (2) The ZIP cluster (J) counts in spoke-okn-geolocation-crosswalks.json were gated on the 978 ZIP nodes that carry a KWG ZipCodeArea reference, but spoke-okn actually has ~42,724 ZIP nodes ALL bearing a bare-ZIP rdfs:label; recomputed on the full set the ZIP joins are far larger - sudokn 12,329 (was 387), ruralkg 4,938 (was 178), dreamkg 53 (was 4) - i.e. spoke-okn is effectively a complete national ZIP/county/state reference and the join is bounded by the PARTNER's coverage, not spoke-okn's. CITY level does not join: spoke-okn's ~67,909 city/place nodes are name slugs with no FIPS/GEOID (see known_non_joins).
cluster_notes.L_county_fips_hub_attachments: Cluster L adds three county-FIPS-keyed members to the SAWGraph spatial world, each reached through a DIFFERENT non-obvious encoding of the same key: geoconnex (hydrology; FIPS as https://geoconnex.us/ref/counties/{FIPS5} reference IRIs on the GNIS county predicate; 3,114 counties to spatialkg / 3,184 to spoke-okn / 51 states), scales (federal court justice data; FIPS as a NUMERIC hasIdbCounty literal with the leading zero dropped, sentinel 88888 removed; 3,029 to spatialkg / 3,096 to spoke-okn), and nikg (Philadelphia/Chicago neighborhood incidents; FIPS in a phila.gov-rewritten KWG sfWithin IRI; 2 counties). All three join on the SAME county-FIPS key the K-cluster uses, so they also meet ruralkg (K2), sockg (K3) and each other at the county level via the hub. Three base-file verdicts are thereby corrected: scales (was a geographic island on the unpopulated fips:CountyCode field), nikg (was 'no geographic key at all'), and geoconnex (only non-joins were recorded; those non-joins on S2 cells and PWS reference IRIs remain valid, but the county-FIPS key is a separate, working route to the hub).
cluster_notes.M_mesh_vocabulary: Cluster M attaches biobricks-mesh - a standalone NLM MeSH vocabulary whose entities are their own id.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/{ID} descriptor IRIs and which carries no outbound xref of its own - to the federation via TWO complementary routes. M1 (broad, indirect): ubergraph cross-references 10,004 MeSH ids as oboInOwl:hasDbXref 'MESH:{ID}' literals; 9,463 of biobricks-mesh's descriptors match (8,202 MONDO disease, 1,051 UBERON anatomy, 83 CL cell type), so through MONDO biobricks-mesh joins the disease cluster A (oard-kg/rdkg/prokn/nde and, via DOID<->MONDO, spoke-okn's disease ontology). M2 (narrow, direct): spoke-okn itself MeSH-tags ~165 nodes through mesh_ids / mesh_list - 155 Disease + 10 SDoH - all matching biobricks-mesh, with NO bridge needed. The two routes are not redundant: M2 uniquely reaches spoke-okn's SDoH (social-determinants) nodes, which have no MONDO term and so are invisible to M1. Watch the IRI gotchas: ubergraph uses 'MESH:{ID}' literals (M1) and spoke-okn uses HTTPS mesh IRIs vs biobricks-mesh's HTTP (M2) - both need bare-id normalization. Overlap check (M2 vs spoke-okn's DOID disease join): all 180 spoke-okn Disease nodes are DOID-identified and 159 also carry a MeSH tag, so for diseases M2 and the DOID join hit the same entities (M2 supplies a MeSH<->DOID map on shared nodes, not new diseases); only the 10 SDoH nodes are unique to M2. Cross-route validation (M2 vs M1): bridging spoke's DOID->MONDO via ubergraph, 118/164 of the spoke MeSH<->DOID disease pairs are exactly corroborated by ubergraph's independent MeSH->MONDO xref, 32 are cases ubergraph has no MeSH (M2 adds coverage), and only 14 disagree - all semantically adjacent (organism-vs-disease or parent/child granularity), no flat errors. MeSH is a high-confidence bridge for exact ids but approximate at the leaves, especially for infections; see M2.cross_route_validation.
cluster_notes.N_fiokg_spatial_and_naics: fiokg (SAWGraph FRS KG; EPA Facility Registry Service) attaches to the federation on TWO axes. (1) SPATIAL - it is a full SAWGraph spatial leaf: every facility links via owl:sameAs to native KWG/STKO resource IRIs (the same stack as spatialkg, sawgraph, hydrologykg, sockg), so attachment needs NO rewrite. It carries 681,108 S2 Level-13 cells (681,045 in spatialkg - the federation's largest S2 join, N1) and 3,040 clean county-FIPS KWG admin-region IRIs (3,031 in spatialkg, N2; 3,032 in spoke-okn, N3). It is the FOURTH and largest S2 leaf on the hub and, being national, the only facility-scale one. It attaches ONLY at the county + S2 levels (0 state KWG IRIs). Because fiokg and sawgraph are both KWG-S2 leaves and fiokg is national while sawgraph is Maine, they OVERLAP directly in 4,712 Maine cells (N6) - a true leaf-to-leaf join, not just a hub rendezvous - which is valuable since fiokg flags 188,057 EPA-PFAS-Facility instances against sawgraph's PFAS samples. (2) INDUSTRY - fiokg classifies facilities with NAICS (ofPrimaryIndustry / ofSecondaryIndustry -> http://w3id.org/fio/v1/naics#NAICS-{6-digit}); the bare 6-digit code joins the manufacturing/supply-chain cluster (I): 64 of sudokn's 66 codes (N4) and all 301 of securechainkg's codes (N5) are contained in fiokg's 3,842-code national span. The join is at the industry-CLASS level (shared NAICS code), not on facility/company instances, exactly as securechainkg<->sudokn (I1). DATA-QUALITY NOTE: of fiokg's 3,301 distinct admin-region owl:sameAs objects, 261 (256 three-digit + 5 four-digit) are leading-zero-truncated and do not match the zero-padded KWG hub form; filter to the 5-digit suffix for the county join (see known_non_joins).
cluster_notes.O_ufokn_s2: ufokn (Urban Flooding OKN) attaches to the SAWGraph spatial hub on S2 Level-13 cells, but via a non-obvious encoding that defeated the base-file scan. Its S2 cells are blank nodes (typed schema:PropertyValue + ufokn's own kwg:S2Cell ontology class), not KWG resource IRIs, and the cell id lives in schema:value as a bare decimal 64-bit integer - the IDENTICAL value spatialkg uses as the suffix of its S2Cell_Level13 node IRI. Rebuilding s2.level13.{value} and joining to spatialkg's typed nodes is direct (no value rewrite). The base file recorded ufokn as 'unprofiled-large' and 'S2 = 0'; both are superseded here (the 0 was a direct typed-NODE join against blank nodes, which can never match; the timeout was an unbounded scan of ~11.7M S2 nodes). Re-profiled with a type-bounded sub-SELECT + object-shape regex filter as the base file advised. All three samples show 100% containment of ufokn level-13 cells in spatialkg, so this is a near-complete leaf attachment whose exact cardinality just isn't enumerable within the endpoint's time limit.
cluster_notes.P_pubchem_cid: Cluster P attaches biobricks-pubchem-annotations - a 14.4M-compound PubChem annotation graph (oa:Annotation nodes whose oa:hasTarget / dc:subject objects are http://rdf.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubchem/compound/CID{n} IRIs, each annotation carrying free-text hazard/toxicity/use text on its body) - to the federation via PubChem CID. The original profiling pass recorded it as an island because no chemical-cluster KG (biobricks-ice/tox21/toxcast, keyed on CAS+DTXSID) and not identifier-mappings (CID-free) carries a CID. That pass missed spoke-okn: its 798 biolink:ChemicalEntity nodes expose the CID as oboInOwl:hasDbXref objects in http://identifiers.org/pubchem.compound/{n} form (762 distinct), a sibling IRI form of the same CID. A naive IRI join returns 0 (form drift: rdf.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/.../CID{n} vs identifiers.org/pubchem.compound/{n}); strip both to the bare numeric CID to join. Verified exact 2026-06-11: 762/762 of spoke-okn's CID-bearing compounds (100%) have >=1 biobricks annotation - e.g. Atrazine CID 2256, Diuron CID 3120, Phenytoin CID 1775, Fluorouracil CID 3385. spoke-okn is the ONLY federation partner on PubChem CID. NB spoke-okn ALSO references PubChem as InChIKey IRIs (762 ChemicalEntity node IRIs + 55 INTERACTS_CiC/PARTOF_CpC edge objects, http://rdf.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubchem/inchikey/{KEY}); that is a DIFFERENT key and does NOT match biobricks' CID - use the hasDbXref CID route, not the node-IRI InChIKey route. This SUPERSEDES the base file's biobricks-pubchem-annotations island / PubChem-CID known_non_join.
cluster_notes.BH_biohealth_umls: Cluster BH attaches biohealth (Bio-Health KG, UVA; ~110M triples, ~251k entities) to the federation. biohealth keys EVERY entity on its UMLS CUI carried as the node's OWN IRI (https://biohealthkg.proto-okn.net/kg/node/C{cui}), typed generically biolink:Entity, with custom schema predicates (COMPLICATES, treats, affects, causes, coexists_with, location_of) whose objects are again CUIs; it carries NO outbound ontology xref of its own. It therefore reaches the federation only through ubergraph's INBOUND UMLS cross-references: ubergraph oboInOwl:hasDbXref 'UMLS:{cui}' lands on MONDO disease (10,087 of them are biohealth CUIs), HP phenotype (4,828) and UBERON anatomy (2,148) - the 498 other UMLS-xref'd terms are blank nodes. Rebuild the biohealth node IRI from the bare CUI (CONCAT('https://biohealthkg.proto-okn.net/kg/node/', ?cui)) to point-check membership; drive joins from the bounded ubergraph bridge set (or an inner DISTINCT of the partner KG's ontology terms) because biohealth is too large to scan unbounded and times out. Verified attachments: BH1 rdkg (MONDO, 9,122), BH2 prokn (HP, 4,284), BH3 spoke-okn (MONDO->DOID two-hop, 173 of ~180), BH4 oard-kg MONDO disease (1,796), BH5 oard-kg HP phenotype (4,549, the largest phenotype join), BH6 nde (MONDO, 2,760), BH7 biomarkerkg (MONDO->DOID two-hop, 620), BH8 gene-expression-atlas-okn (HP, 13). DOID-keyed partners (spoke-okn, biomarkerkg) need the extra MONDO skos:exactMatch DOID hop because DOID is NOT UMLS-xref'd in ubergraph. CEILING: there is NO CHEBI/UniProt/NCBIGene/NCIT UMLS xref, so biohealth can NOT crosswalk on chemicals, genes or proteins - only disease, phenotype and anatomy. The UBERON anatomy axis (2,148 CUIs) is now VERIFIED (2026-06-23): biohealth joins GXA on UBERON (BH9, 249 of GXA's 362 tissue terms via biolink:has_attribute) and spoke-genelab on UBERON (BH10, 35 of 42 via INVESTIGATED_ASiA). spoke-okn does NOT store these as raw obo/UBERON_ terms (0). Cell Ontology (CL) is NOT a biohealth axis - ubergraph UMLS->CL = 0 (e.g. spoke-genelab's 7 CL cell types reach 0 biohealth nodes). biohealth is also a LABEL-BRIDGED member of the taxon_hub for organisms (no NCBITaxon ids; see taxon_hub.$note) - that route is name-based and fragile, but the six non-zero label-match pairs (BH11-BH16) were re-verified and promoted into verified_crosswalks on 2026-06-25 with shared_key 'NCBITaxon (biohealth label)'. Verified 2026-06-23.
cluster_notes.AN_anatomy_uberon: Cluster AN is the Anatomy (UBERON) cluster. Anatomy-carrying KGs that store raw obo/UBERON_ IRIs: spoke-genelab (42 terms on INVESTIGATED_ASiA, biolink:AnatomicalEntity; plus 7 Cell Ontology CL cell types on INVESTIGATED_ASiCT) and gene-expression-atlas-okn (362 tissue terms on biolink:has_attribute). They join DIRECTLY on the shared UBERON IRI: AN1 spoke-genelab<->GXA = 27 shared terms (no bridge). biohealth also participates but only through the ubergraph UMLS bridge (its 2,148 UBERON CUIs): BH9 biohealth<->GXA (249) and BH10 biohealth<->spoke-genelab (35). spoke-okn does NOT carry these raw UBERON terms (verified 0 in both subject and object position), so it is not part of this cluster. ubergraph is the anatomy hub (full UBERON + CL with subClassOf* for clade/part-of expansion and the oboInOwl:hasDbXref UMLS/MeSH cross-references). CL (Cell Ontology) SUB-AXIS: cell types are carried as raw obo/CL_ IRIs by gene-expression-atlas-okn (223 terms, biolink:has_attribute), prokn (cell types as rdf:subject of reified marker-gene statements) and spoke-genelab (7 terms, INVESTIGATED_ASiCT). Verified CL joins: AN2 GXA<->prokn = 31 (the substantive one), AN3 spoke-genelab<->GXA = 4, AN4 spoke-genelab<->prokn = 1. spoke-okn has no CL (0); biohealth has no CL concepts (ubergraph UMLS->CL = 0), so CL is not a biohealth axis.
cluster_notes.R_digcfdekg: Cluster R attaches digcfdekg (CFDE REVEAL KG; statistically inferred genomic evidence graph, PIGEAN + EAGGL) to the federation and is the first integration of the newly added rdkg & digcfdekg pair. digcfdekg is NOW MATERIALIZED at the endpoint (this SUPERSEDES the base file's 'digcfdekg unmaterialized / zero triples' known_non_join, moved to superseded_non_joins). It models reified rdf:Statement associations with edge types geneToTrait, geneToFactor, geneSetToTrait, geneSetToFactor, traitToFactor, geneInGeneSet (each exposed BOTH as a direct triple ?s pred ?o AND as a reified node carrying schema/weight = association probability, dcterms:source PIGEAN|EAGGL, schema/scoreType - use the direct form for join-key extraction). Join keys: genes as Entrez node IRIs (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/{entrez}, 21,710 genes) and traits as EFO (1,687) + Orphanet (1,526) + MONDO (435) + internal trait nodes (1,476, no external id). GENE attachments live in the C cluster: C10 digcfdekg<->spoke-okn (16,052, identical Entrez IRI), C11 digcfdekg<->spoke-genelab (19,747, identical Entrez IRI), C12 digcfdekg<->rdkg (8,934, ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene <-> identifiers.org/ncbigene rewrite), C13 digcfdekg<->prokn (20,783, Entrez->HGNC via wikidata P351->P354, same bridge as C9). DISEASE attachments live in the A cluster: A25 digcfdekg<->rdkg (1,045), A26 digcfdekg<->oard-kg (402), A27 digcfdekg<->biomarkerkg (123, DOID->MONDO), A28 digcfdekg<->spoke-okn (50, DOID->MONDO), A29 digcfdekg<->gene-expression-atlas-okn (33, direct EFO/Orphanet/MONDO). Because digcfdekg keys diseases mostly on EFO/Orphanet, the disease joins are driven by bridging EFO/Orphanet->MONDO via ubergraph skos:exactMatch (raises the digcfdekg disease set from 435 direct MONDO to 1,634 MONDO terms; direct-only would undercount, e.g. rdkg 180->1,045, oard-kg 37->402). PERFORMANCE: digcfdekg is large and its gene endpoints have very high fan-out - always materialize the DISTINCT key set in an inner SELECT before probing the partner graph; an unbound join over a digcfdekg gene/disease pattern (incl. FILTER EXISTS) OOMs the endpoint at ~210 GB. A full unscoped COUNT(*) and get_schema's class enumeration also exceed endpoint memory - use bounded probes. rdkg's pre-existing joins (A10/A16/A19/A2/BH1/C5/C6/C8/Q1/Q2) are unchanged; C12+A25 are rdkg's only NEW crosswalk (to digcfdekg, complementary gene+disease).
cluster_notes.BH_sdoh: Cluster BH-SDoH connects the Social-Determinants-of-Health layers of biohealth and spoke-okn - the first SDoH crosswalk between them (prior BH3/BH11 link only disease and taxonomy). spoke-okn has a dedicated SDoH class (1,426 concepts) keyed on SNOMED CT concept ids in the node IRI, with geographic prevalence (PREVALENCEIN_SpL, ~3M statements over 1,144 concepts) and a small SDoH->disease layer (ASSOCIATES_SaD, 39 MeSH-co-occurrence statements); only 10 SDoH carry spoke:mesh_ids (the County Health Rankings indicators). biohealth keys every node on a UMLS CUI (node IRI .../node/C{cui}, rdfs:label = concept name, SemMedDB predicates) and carries NO MeSH/SNOMED/MONDO/DOID xref, so the join must route through UMLS. Two complementary routes: BH17 MeSH->UMLS via wikidata P486->P2892 (3 of the 10 MeSH indicators reach a biohealth node - precise, hits the data-rich CHR indicators) and BH18 concept-label match (89 of 1,426 SDoH exact-match a biohealth concept by suffix-stripped label - broad, covers the SNOMED ontology backbone). The ideal key, SNOMED->UMLS, is UNAVAILABLE: the federation wikidata has no P5806 and no graph materializes a UMLS<->SNOMED map (it lives in the UMLS Metathesaurus, not loaded). Loading that map - or having biohealth emit SNOMED xrefs - would turn ~90 label matches into a full ~1,400-concept SDoH join. PERFORMANCE: a case-insensitive label join (LCASE over biohealth's ~250k labels) OOMs/times out; drive from the bounded spoke SDoH side with the bound label and probe biohealth (indexed).
cluster_notes.PB_publications: PB - Publications / bibliographic (DOI). Scholarly DOI is the join key. nasa-gesdisc-kg is a large bibliometric graph (465,143 publications citing/using NASA Earth-science datasets; each with bibo:doi as an http://dx.doi.org/ IRI, plus author ORCID and institution ROR). climatemodelskg carries a DOI literal (https://doi.org/ form) on its 1,910 climate-modeling Paper nodes. Normalize both to the bare lowercase DOI (strip scheme+host, LCASE) and match. PB1 = climatemodelskg x nasa-gesdisc-kg = 651 shared papers (de-islands nasa-gesdisc-kg). The ORCID (author) and ROR (institution) axes on nasa-gesdisc-kg are unexplored bonus bridges to climatemodelskg's authors/affiliations.
cluster_notes.EO_earth_observation: EO - Earth observation instruments & platforms (GCMD name). climatemodelskg NLP-extracts Instrument and Platform mentions from climate-modeling papers (free-text climatepub4kg:name); nasa-gesdisc-kg carries the same as GCMD controlled-vocabulary terms (rdfs:label) in NASA's Global Change Master Directory keyword tree. Lowercase-match the names; the join is self-cleaning (only standardized names match). EO1 = Instrument (115), EO2 = Platform (70). Both are climatemodelskg x nasa-gesdisc-kg and complement PB1 (DOI, 651) - a second, orthogonal edge connecting climate-modeling literature to NASA GES DISC's Earth-observation catalogue. Label bridge (fragile at the margins - a few generic terms like LIDAR/Aircraft slip in), comparable to the taxon/SDoH label bridges.
