spatial_hub_note.topology: spatialkg is the national S2 grid + admin-region hub. Its S2 Level-13 leaves are sawgraph (Maine; D2), hydrologykg (Illinois; D1), sockg (multi-state; H1), fiokg (national; N1) and now ufokn (continental US; O1). Leaves that share a state co-occupy cells (e.g. fiokg<->sawgraph in Maine, N6); otherwise they meet through the hub. spoke-okn and the cluster K/L members attach at the county and state admin-region levels (national county coverage).
spatial_hub_note.spoke_okn_attachment: CONFIRMED: spoke-okn attaches to the spatialkg hub via county FIPS (3,122; K1) and state FIPS (51; K4), by rebuilding the KWG administrativeRegion.USA.{FIPS} IRI from spoke-okn's bare-FIPS node IRIs. It does NOT attach via ZIP (spatialkg has no ZipCodeArea nodes) or S2 cell (spoke-okn has none of its own). spoke-okn is now a THIRD admin-region-keyed member of the SAWGraph spatial world alongside sockg, sawgraph and hydrologykg - and the only one with national county coverage.
spatial_hub_note.cluster_L_county_members: Cluster L adds three more county-FIPS-keyed members to this hub, each via a different non-obvious encoding of the same key: geoconnex (hydrology; 3,114 counties to spatialkg / 3,184 to spoke-okn / 51 states; L1-L3), scales (federal-court justice data via numeric hasIdbCounty, sentinel 88888 dropped; 3,029 to spatialkg / 3,096 to spoke-okn; L4-L5), and nikg (Philadelphia 42101 + Cook/Chicago 17031 via phila.gov-rewritten KWG sfWithin IRIs; L6-L7). All join on the same county-FIPS key as cluster K, so they also meet ruralkg (K2), sockg (K3), spoke-okn (K1) and each other at the county level.
spatial_hub_note.fiokg_attachment: CONFIRMED: fiokg attaches to the spatialkg hub via S2 Level-13 cells (681,045; N1 - the largest S2 join in the federation) and county FIPS (3,031 AdministrativeRegion_2; N2), both in native KWG resource IRI form requiring NO rewrite. It does NOT attach via state (no KWG AdministrativeRegion_1 IRIs) or ZIP. fiokg is the FOURTH S2-keyed leaf on the hub alongside sawgraph (Maine), hydrologykg (Illinois) and sockg (multi-state soil carbon) - and, with national facility coverage, by far the largest. It also meets spoke-okn at the county level (3,032; N3, spoke-okn's national county coverage). Unusually, fiokg and the sawgraph leaf OVERLAP directly in 4,712 Maine S2 cells (N6) rather than only meeting through the hub.
spatial_hub_note.ufokn_attachment: CONFIRMED: ufokn attaches to the spatialkg hub via S2 Level-13 cells (O1), making it the FIFTH S2-keyed leaf alongside sawgraph, hydrologykg, sockg and fiokg. Unlike the others, ufokn's S2 cells are BLANK NODES (not KWG resource IRIs); the cell id is the bare decimal 64-bit integer in schema:value, which is rebuilt into spatialkg's s2.level13.{id} IRI for a direct join (no rewrite). All sampled level-13 cells are present in spatialkg (100% containment across 1k/8k/20k-cell samples), so the attachment is near-complete; the exact count is not enumerable within the 120s limit (verified_count 7,670 is a sampled lower bound). A county/state admin-region or geometry route for ufokn was NOT profiled and is left open. ufokn also carries finer S2 Level-18 cells that nest inside the level-13 hub cells but do not attach to the level-13 hub directly.

methodology_note: OKN FEDERATION GOTCHAS used throughout cluster L (learned while verifying these joins): (1) a constant-IRI constraint in a remote GRAPH block can silently return 0 - e.g. '?loc a <https://schema.org/AdministrativeArea>' returns 0 on spoke-okn even though '?loc a ?type' returns the nodes with ?type = that exact IRI; match the county/state nodes by their IRI PATTERN (REGEX on the node IRI) instead of by a bound rdf:type IRI. (2) A VALUES- or BIND-injected IRI is NOT reliably pushed down into a remote GRAPH block, so 'BIND(IRI(...)) AS ?loc . GRAPH <other-kg> { ?loc a ?t }' also returns 0. (3) The reliable cross-graph join is on a BARE STRING KEY: extract the 5-digit county FIPS (or 2-digit state FIPS) as an xsd:string on EACH side independently (each inside its own DISTINCT sub-SELECT scoped to one named graph) and intersect the two sub-SELECTs on that shared ?fips variable. Never use a cross-graph FILTER(STR(?a)=?b) - it returns 0 (same gotcha the base file records for K1). CLUSTER N ADDENDUM: fiokg's owl:sameAs predicate carries ~681k S2-cell objects, so any scan touching the whole predicate (CONTAINS over all of it, or joining two heavy graphs through it) can hit the 120s endpoint limit; scope each side in its own DISTINCT sub-SELECT and keep the partner light - for spoke-okn (N3) rebuild the .../location/{FIPS5} node IRI from fiokg's extracted FIPS and bind it as the same variable rather than regex-scanning spoke-okn. For NAICS (N4/N5) a direct IRI join is 0 (each KG mints the classifier IRI differently); extract the bare numeric code on each side and intersect. CLUSTER O ADDENDUM (ufokn): ufokn's S2 cells are BLANK NODES typed schema:PropertyValue + its own <https://stko-kwg.geog.ucsb.edu/lod/ontology#S2Cell> class (NOT spatialkg's S2Cell_Level13 node-type IRI), so the base file's direct typed-NODE join returns 0 by construction - there is no shared node IRI. The shared key is the schema:value LITERAL (bare decimal 64-bit S2 id), joined by rebuilding spatialkg's s2.level13.{value} IRI; that BIND/CONCAT IRI DOES push down into the spatialkg block here (verified), unlike gotcha (2) elsewhere. Two further traps: (a) a CONSTANT predicate on these blank nodes silently returns 0 - '?cell <https://schema.org/value> ?v' yields nothing though '?cell ?p ?v' returns ?p = that exact IRI with the value; read the value via a VARIABLE predicate and select it by object SHAPE (isLiteral && REGEX(STR(?val),'^[0-9]{18,20}$')) rather than by a bound predicate. (b) LARGE-GRAPH: ~11.7M S2-typed nodes; any unbounded DISTINCT/FILTER over the class times out at 120s (>=60k-cell bounded samples can too). Scope ufokn in an inner 'SELECT ?cell ... LIMIT N' sub-SELECT first, then pull+shape-filter the value, then join to the light spatialkg side. Level-18 values harmlessly fail the level-13 membership test, so no name/level filter is needed for a correct level-13 intersection.

identifier-mappings does not carry identifiers.org/cas/ or identifiers.org/pubchem.compound/ IRIs (bound lookups returned zero). Use the ubergraph CHEBI route (B2) to bridge the chemical clusters, not identifier-mappings/wikidata. PROFILED 2026-06-18: identifier-mappings is a LINGUISTIC/lexical mapping graph, NOT a biomedical one - its skos:exactMatch payload is Latin lemmas (lila-erc), WordNet, PropBank/Framester semantic roles and Getty ULAN. It carries NO biological identifiers (no UniProt/RefSeq/Entrez/Ensembl/CAS/PubChem/MONDO), so it cannot bridge any bio KG (e.g. evoweb RefSeq -> UniProt).

find_crosswalks returns empty: no mapping predicates, no ontology/identifier node IRIs, no domain-predicate ids. EvoWeb (co-evolving genes) encodes its members as NCBI RefSeq PROTEIN IRIs (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/protein/WP_xxxxxxxxx.1 - bacterial non-redundant accessions) grouped into SKOS Collections by a free-text functional label; no UniProt/Entrez/Ensembl id and no taxon. INDIRECT-BRIDGE ATTEMPTS (2026-06-18) ALL FAIL: (1) identifier-mappings carries only LINGUISTIC mappings (Latin lemmas/lila, WordNet, PropBank/Framester, Getty ULAN) - zero protein/gene content; (2) wikidata returns nothing for evoweb's WP_ accessions (bacterial non-redundant RefSeq proteins are not itemized in Wikidata); (3) ubergraph carries no protein individuals. No federation graph mirrors the WP_ RefSeq protein IRI, so there is no bridge to the UniProt protein hub. Confirmed island. NAME/LABEL ROUTE also tried 2026-06-18 and FAILS: evoweb has 7,015 distinct cluster labels (RefSeq functional product names, e.g. "hypothetical protein" 332k members, "ABC transporter permease", "MFS transporter", "TetR/AcrR family transcriptional regulator") - generic bacterial function descriptors, not protein identities. Exact case-insensitive label match to the protein KGs returns 0: prokn 0, biobricks-aopwiki 0, spoke-okn 0 (they label proteins by gene symbol or eukaryotic UniProt name, a different string namespace). ncipidkg labels proteins by gene symbol (e.g. "Gam1"), also no overlap. Even a fuzzy match would only collide generic family names across non-homologous proteins, not establish identity. No usable name/label join. RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-01 after the scales/oard-kg/evoweb entities.csv update added two evoweb predicates: connectedTo (Collection->Collection intra-graph cluster-network edges) and secondaryComponent (points to evoweb's OWN https://purl.org/okn/frink/kg/evoweb/schema/NNN_N_NNNN IRIs - opaque internal cluster ids, not an external catalog) - both are internal structure, neither adds an external identifier. skos:member is still the WP_ RefSeq protein accession. Fresh federated lookups of evoweb's actual WP_ accessions returned 0 in both universal hubs: wikidata P637 (RefSeq protein id) and identifier-mappings. Still a confirmed island.

spoke-okn's ~67,909 city/place nodes (.../location/{name-slug}, labels like 'Outside city limits') carry NO FIPS place code, GEOID, or other external identifier - only a name. A city-level join would have to be on the city NAME string, which is unreliable across the federation (same name in many states, inconsistent casing/abbreviation, 'Outside city limits' placeholders), so there is no clean key-based city crosswalk. Use the county (K1-K3) or state (K4-K5) FIPS level for reliable joins; drop to ZIP (cluster J) for finer geography.

(1) productCode = 953 distinct FDA 3-letter device-classification codes (LXH 392, HRX 267, GEI 226, DYB 213, ...) - an FDA-only scheme that NO federation KG carries (not sudokn / fiokg / securechainkg NAICS, not any biomedical id). (2) label = free-text FDA report descriptions on the device IRIs (medicaldevice.com/resource/device/{name}), e.g. ': PUMP, INFUSION, INSULIN, TO BE USED WITH INVASIVE GLUCOSE SENSOR', '#01-04 LINEAR MOTION ADJUSTABLE STIRRUPS', '@CRUTCH, ALUMINUM, ADULT TALL' - uppercase brand / model / part-number strings, NOT controlled concept names, so unlike the OBO / UMLS / audience-term label bridges that DO work (phaseskg SS2, dreamkg SS1, spoke-okn SDoH) they exact-match nothing and substring-match only noise. eventType is Death / Injury / Malfunction / Other / No-answer (no MONDO/HP). The only conceivable route is OUT-OF-FEDERATION: map the 953 product codes through the external FDA Product Classification database (code -> device type -> medical specialty -> NAICS), which no OKN graph materializes. Island.

Of fiokg's 3,301 distinct administrativeRegion.USA owl:sameAs objects, 256 have a 3-digit suffix and 5 have a 4-digit suffix (e.g. .../administrativeRegion.USA.123, .../administrativeRegion.USA.6061) - county FIPS that lost one or two leading zeros, presumably via numeric handling upstream. These do NOT match spatialkg's zero-padded administrativeRegion.USA.{FIPS5} nodes verbatim and are excluded from the N2 count (3,031). They are NOT a different geography - they are damaged encodings of counties already partly covered by the clean 5-digit set. A zero-pad-and-rebuild recovery is conceivable but UNVERIFIED (ambiguous: a 3-digit '123' could pad to several states) and was not pursued; the clean 5-digit county key (N2/N3) is the reliable route.

known_non_joins.attempted_key: S2 Level-13 cell (direct leaf-to-leaf, also tried hydrologykg)
known_non_joins.diagnosis: ufokn IS an S2 Level-13 leaf (O1) and directly co-locates with the NATIONAL leaf fiokg (O2: 2,461 shared cells in a 4,267-cell sample, 58%). But against the SINGLE-STATE leaves sawgraph (Maine) and hydrologykg (Illinois) the same ufokn sample shows 0 shared cells - the sampled ufokn region (geohash 9q/9mvu) does not fall in ME/IL. A global check is INFEASIBLE within tool limits: ufokn stores S2 as 11.7M schema:value property nodes and its https-form schema.org predicates force variable-predicate scans (no object-index use), so both join directions time out; the only feasible bounded query (limit ufokn to ~5k nodes) is region-locked to wherever the scan starts. So ufokn<->sawgraph and ufokn<->hydrologykg are UNVERIFIED - they are non-zero only if ufokn happens to cover a Maine/Illinois metro; assert via the spatialkg hub. ufokn has no label/id/county key to fall back on (Place names are geohash strings, identifiers are ufokn-internal). Checked 2026-06-19.

known_non_joins.result: 0 shared cells in a 40,000-cell sample; full check infeasible

Both attach INDEPENDENTLY to spatialkg (ufokn O1 = 97,087 cells; hydrologykg D1 = 106,138 cells), but they do NOT share L13 cells: 0 exact matches across 40,000 sampled ufokn cells intersected against hydrologykg's FULL 106,138-cell set (also 0 in 300 / 2,000 / 3,000-cell samples, both storage orders). REFINES the ufokn<->sawgraph record's 'hydrologykg = Illinois, outside ufokn's region' note: they actually DO overlap regionally - hydrologykg is mostly S2 face 4 (85,921 of 106,138 cells; face-4 range [9.789e18, 9.936e18]) and the sampled ufokn cells are all face 4 in [9.813e18, 9.821e18], i.e. INSIDE hydrologykg's range - yet no identical L13 (~1 km2) cell coincides. ufokn maps urban-flood infrastructure and hydrologykg maps streams / waterbodies / wells: different feature types that rarely occupy the same 1 km2 cell even when co-located. A global exact count is infeasible (ufokn ~11.7M S2 schema:value nodes; its https schema.org predicates force variable-predicate scans that 429 / time out). Deep dive 2026-06-27: spoke-genelab keys its Studies on NASA OSDR accessions (node/OSD-1 'Drosophila immune function in altered gravity', node/OSD-100 'Rodent Research 1', ...) and Missions on OSDR mission ids, with project_title/space_program/flight_program/dates. BUT the FOUNDIN_CfL chemicals are keyed on ChEMBL (identifiers.org/chembl.compound/CHEMBL...), which NO other federation KG uses (sawgraph/biobricks use CAS; spoke's own drug layer uses CHEBI/DrugBank/PubChem-CID), and the EnvironmentalFeature is only 2 label-based PM terms. So spoke-okn's environmental-exposure layer has no direct chemical crosswalk; it could reach the toxicology cluster only indirectly (ChEMBL -> CHEBI -> CAS via the existing B2 CHEBI<->CAS bridge). spoke-okn's environmental exposure and disease prevalence share the same AdministrativeArea (county FIPS), enabling an INTRA-KG exposure<->disease analysis and a spatial join to sawgraph/fiokg on county FIPS (K/N), but on geography, not a new chemical/environmental id.

known_non_joins.attempted_key: CHEBI (extend prokn's ChEMBL/InChIKey chemical hub to rdkg's CHEBI-keyed chemicals)
known_non_joins.result: no shared key (prokn carries no CHEBI)

So the two share NO chemical identifier: prokn is ChEMBL / InChIKey / PubChem-keyed, rdkg is CHEBI / DrugBank-keyed, with no overlapping scheme. A prokn<->rdkg chemical join would need a ChEMBL/InChIKey<->CHEBI bridge (wikidata P592/P683 or ubergraph), not a direct key. NOTE: prokn DOES reach chemicals elsewhere - it joins spoke-okn on InChIKey (C11-inchikey-spokeokn-prokn, 143), and could attach near-totally to the PubChem annotation backdrop biobricks-pubchem-annotations on PubChem CID (both carry pubchem/compound/{CID}), but that 14.4M-compound backdrop join is trivial and does not verify within the endpoint limit. IMPORTANT: this non-join is the CHEMICAL / CHEBI axis ONLY - prokn and rdkg DO share direct join keys on MONDO (disease) and Entrez (gene) and are joinable there (they just have no materialized pairwise crosswalk, connecting through hubs like oard-kg/ubergraph); do NOT read this record as 'prokn and rdkg do not join'. Checked 2026-07-12.

known_non_joins.attempted_key: MeSH descriptor id (nikg declares two mesh_* classes: https://metadata.phila.gov/mesh_D000091368 and mesh_D005842)
known_non_joins.result: mechanically resolvable (2/2 descriptors match) but SEMANTICALLY EMPTY - not a justice<->biomedical bridge
known_non_joins.diagnosis: nikg's two mesh_* classes are phila.gov-namespaced LOCAL class URIs with a MeSH descriptor id baked into the local name (extract with BIND(IRI(CONCAT('http://id.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/', STRAFTER(STR(?cls),'mesh_'))))). Both resolve cleanly in biobricks-mesh - but they are D000091368 = 'Census Tract' (MeSH tree E05/N06, epidemiologic methods & health-care statistics) and D005842 = 'Geographic Locations' (tree Z01, Geographicals). NEITHER carries any disease, injury or firearm semantics: nikg simply borrowed two MeSH GEOGRAPHIC descriptors as class URIs for its census tracts (1,142 entities) and incident locations (30,089 entities) - the same things already typed by its own metadata.phila.gov/CensusTract and /Location classes. The join adds zero information (it tells you a census tract is a 'Census Tract'), and no MeSH hierarchy walk from these terms reaches anything health-related that applies to nikg's incidents. Verified live 2026-07-12. Recorded PRECISELY BECAUSE the class names look like a biomedical bridge at a glance and will otherwise be re-proposed. If nikg later adds real health descriptors, the local-name extraction rule above is the way in. NOTE: this is a MeSH-axis non-join only - nikg joins the federation on geography (county FIPS, S2), so do NOT read it as 'nikg does not join'.

After bare-CID normalization the join is exact: 762/762 of spoke-okn's CID-bearing compounds match a biobricks annotation (verified 2026-06-11). The CAS->synonym-text thread remains the only (still fragile) route to the CAS cluster, but biobricks-pubchem-annotations is no longer an island: it attaches to the chemical world through spoke-okn on PubChem CID.

CORRECTIONS vs the base file: scales and nikg are NO LONGER islands - they attach to the SAWGraph spatial hub on county FIPS (cluster L4-L7); and ruralkg, dreamkg and sudokn join spoke-okn on geography (ZIP - cluster J; county FIPS - cluster K). Current islands below: medical-device-kg and nasa-gesdisc-kg are detailed under known_non_joins. (phaseskg was listed here as a pure T-Box ontology with no instance data, but as of 2026-07-11 its psychosocial/aging class labels bridge biohealth on 8 SDoH concepts - SS2-label-phaseskg-biohealth - so it is now a thin_thread, not a full island.) UPDATE (2026-06-11 profiling pass): biobricks-pubchem-annotations added as an island - it is keyed solely on PubChem CID, which no federation KG materializes (detailed under known_non_joins). Its sibling biobricks-mesh is NOT an island: it attaches to ubergraph (and thereby the disease cluster) on MeSH descriptor ids - cluster M1. UPDATE (2026-06-11 fiokg pass): fiokg is NOT an island - it joins the SAWGraph spatial hub on S2 cells + county FIPS (N1-N3, N6) and the manufacturing cluster on NAICS (N4-N5). UPDATE (2026-06-11 ufokn pass): ufokn is NOT an island and was never listed as one (it was 'unprofiled-large'); it attaches to the SAWGraph spatial hub on S2 Level-13 cells (cluster O1), so its base-file 'unprofiled-large' and 'S2 = 0' verdicts are superseded (see superseded_non_joins). UPDATE (2026-06-11 PubChem-CID pass): biobricks-pubchem-annotations is NO LONGER an island. It joins spoke-okn on PubChem CID (cluster P1): spoke-okn carries 762 identifiers.org/pubchem.compound/{CID} ids via oboInOwl:hasDbXref - missed by the original pass, which only checked the CAS cluster and identifier-mappings. Exact join 762/762 (100%); the prior 'PubChem-CID island' known_non_join is moved to superseded_non_joins. UPDATE (2026-06-19 sudokn pass): sudokn now attaches DIRECTLY to spatialkg, not only via spoke-okn ZIP (J1). It joins the admin hierarchy at STATE level on locatedInState label -> AdministrativeRegion_1/hasFIPS (SU1, state_FIPS; 42,606 sites / 25,887 companies / 51 regions, live SPARQL), and reaches county/S2 grain via the COMPUTED crosswalk SU2 (S2_L13), where the mcp-okn s2_bridge derives each site's S2 cell from its lat/long at query time. sudokn therefore reaches the SAWGraph spatial hub directly.
thin_threads: ruralkg substance-abuse layer -> chemical identity via Wikidata (characterized 2026-07-11; refines the old '~23 Wikidata links' note). Its 23 Substance nodes (NSDUH/NIBRS drugs of abuse: Alcohol, Cocaine, Crack, Heroin, Ketamine, LSD, MDMA, Marijuana, Methamphetamine, Nicotine, PCP, Psilocybin, Mescaline, DMT, ...) carry clean rdfs:label + a Wikidata QID on owl:sameAs / skos:exactMatch / wikidataId. Through the federation wikidata graph, 7 of the specific compounds resolve to standard chemical ids - e.g. Cocaine -> CHEBI:27958 / PubChem 446220 / CAS 50-36-2 / ChEMBL370805; Heroin -> CHEBI:27808; Ketamine -> CHEBI:6121; MDMA -> CHEBI:1391; also Psilocybin, Mescaline, DMT (the rest are drug CLASSES - Hallucinogen/Stimulant/Sedative/Inhalant - or QIDs lacking chemical props). BUT the chain DEAD-ENDS at the ontology backbone: all 7 CHEBI terms exist in ubergraph (cocaine/heroin/ketamine/...), yet NO federation DATA-KG carries these recreational drugs - spoke-okn PubChem 0, spoke-okn/rdkg CHEBI 0, biobricks-ice CAS 0 (the federation's chemical KGs are environmental toxicology + biomedical drugs, not drugs of abuse). So ruralkg's substances are chemically well-identified and reach ubergraph's CHEBI hierarchy, but have no chemical DATA partner - a valid identifier bridge with no positive KG-to-KG join. (ruralkg also has 7 DrugBank drug IRIs that could touch rdkg DrugBank.)
ruralkg: censusCounty (KWG administrativeRegion.USA.{FIPS}) joins spoke-okn (K2) and the spatialkg hub; postalCode joins spoke-okn ZIPs (J2).
dreamkg: schema:postalCode joins spoke-okn on 53 Philadelphia ZIPs (J3).

sudokn: hasZipcodeValue joins spoke-okn on 12,329 ZIPs (J1); ALSO attaches directly to spatialkg at state level (SU1, locatedInState->AdministrativeRegion_1/hasFIPS, state_FIPS) and at county/S2 grain via the computed s2_bridge crosswalk (SU2, S2_L13).

phaseskg: a small OBO-style ontology (the PHASES 'Promoting Healthy Aging through Semantic Enrichment' vocabulary, ~377 typed entities) with NO instance data. It is built on OBO upper ontologies (BFO, IAO, OMO, RO, GO, MF, MFOEM, OGMS, OBI); 23 of its imported non-PHASES OBO terms also exist (as labelled classes) in ubergraph - an ontology-scaffolding overlap on identical obo IRIs, NOT a data join. It carries no MONDO/HP/DOID/CHEBI/gene/geographic identifiers. UPDATE (2026-07-11): NO LONGER a full island - its psychosocial / aging class LABELS bridge biohealth on 8 SDoH concepts (loneliness, social isolation, social withdrawal, social detachment, shyness, alienation, reminiscence therapy, self-efficacy) via biohealth's UMLS concept names - see SS2-label-phaseskg-biohealth. Still no instance data and no identifier join beyond the ubergraph ontology-scaffolding overlap; the label bridge is fragile and a curated lower bound.

wildlifekn: 5,205 reified observation Statements over 657 Location nodes, 303 Bird_name and 97 Amphibian_name nodes. Species are stored as scientific-name LABEL strings WITH taxonomic authority (e.g. 'Ardea alba Linnaeus, 1758') - NO NCBITaxon IRIs. VERIFIED 2026-06-18: stripping the authority to the bare binomial and matching ubergraph NCBITaxon rdfs:label resolves 339 species to NCBITaxon IRIs, attaching wildlifekn to the taxon hub (now a LABEL-BRIDGED member; see taxon_hub + D11/D12). Exact-id pairwise overlap: nde 17 (avian-flu reservoirs + disease amphibians), sawgraph 2, spoke-okn 0 (bacterial). The join is fragile (label/binomial agreement; subspecies collapse to species) but reproducible. GEOGRAPHIC route VERIFIED 2026-06-18: Location nodes carry free-text place labels (Florida cities + counties); the county-type ones ("X County") match spatialkg Florida county-subdivision labels and resolve to 63 county FIPS5 codes (label-bridged, Florida-only, city locations excluded) - attaching wildlifekn to the county_FIPS spatial hub (see L8). City-type locations and coordinates remain unmapped.

fiokg <-> ufokn: SUPERSEDED for ufokn - ufokn DOES carry an S2 Level-13 key (in schema:value; cluster O1), so both fiokg (national, N1) and ufokn (continental US, O1) are S2 leaves on the spatialkg hub and meet through it in any shared cell; a DIRECT leaf-to-leaf fiokg<->ufokn S2 count was not separately verified (both graphs are heavy on the S2 predicate; regional sampling makes a direct count unreliable - assert via the hub). The remaining KGs in this thread (nasa-gesdisc-kg / wildlifekn / climatemodelskg) still carry no KWG S2/admin-region key fiokg can meet (per their known_non_joins); fiokg has no confirmed direct spatial join to them.
